definition_zh: 买得起；负担得起；抽得出（时间、精力）；承受得起（后果）；提供、给予
definition_en: to have enough money, time or strength for something, to be able to bear a risk, or to provide something useful
core_image: 把手伸进口袋掂一掂，看还能不能拿得出这一份
scene: 月底的超市里，有人把几样东西放回货架，只留下最必需的。After paying the rent, she could not afford the new coat.
sceneCN: 这里 afford 是「买得起」（第 1 个义项：有足够的钱支付）；句意为付完房租之后，她买不起那件新外套。画面里可辨认的是货架、价签与购物篮。

pos.zh: 及物动词：负担得起；抽得出；承受得起；提供、给予

collocations.zh: 有条件做某事；经得起做某事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「负担得起的；价格合理的」
由 affordable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性；支付能力」
由否定前缀 un- 加 affordable 构成，义为「负担不起的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「可供性」，指物品本身提示的用法

senses.title: To have enough money for something
senses.definition: to have enough money to pay for something without serious difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱支付某物，而且不至于陷入严重困难
senses.example: At today's prices, few families can afford a house in that district.
senses.exampleCN: 按现在的价格，那个区没有几户人家买得起房子。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant 'to carry a thing through'; money sense grew from 'to manage to put out', so affording is managing to meet a price.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词的本义是「把事情办成」，钱义从「拿得出、给得起」长出来，所以 afford 的钱义本质是「勉强付得起这个价」。

senses.title: To have enough time or energy
senses.definition: to be able to spare the time, energy or effort that something needs
senses.definitionCN: 能够腾出某件事所需的时间、精力或力气
senses.example: I can't afford three hours for a meeting this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今天上午我抽不出三个小时去开会。
senses.why: Time is treated as the same kind of resource as money: it can be given out or not given out, so the verb simply changes what is being spent.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当成和钱同一类资源：它可以被拿出，也可以拿不出，动词只是换掉了被花掉的东西，于是表示「抽得出时间」。

senses.title: To be able to bear a result
senses.definition: to be able to do something or accept a result without suffering serious harm
senses.definitionCN: 能够做某事或接受某个结果，而不至于受到严重损害
senses.example: With so few staff, the clinic cannot afford a single mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 人手这么少，诊所一次失误都承受不起。
senses.why: If affording is carrying a burden through, a risk is a burden that must be strong enough to be carried; this is why the verb so often appears in the negative.
senses.whyCN: 既然 afford 的本义是把担子扛过去，风险就是一副必须扛得住的担子，所以这个词常出现在否定式里，表示「承受不起」。

senses.title: To provide or give something
senses.titleCN: 提供；给予（机会、景色、保护）
senses.definition: to give or make available something useful, such as a chance, a view or protection
senses.definitionCN: 给予或使某样有用的东西可以被得到，如机会、景色或保护
senses.example: The wide windows afford a clear view of the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 宽大的窗户让人可以清楚地看到海湾。
senses.why: The oldest layer, 'to further, promote', survives here: a thing affords whatever it puts within your reach.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的那层意思「促成、使向前」在这里保留下来：某样东西提供了你伸手可及的条件，就是 afford。

senses.title: To grant a person something
senses.definition: to spare or grant a person something, especially time or attention, in polite or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 在客气或正式的用法中为某人腾出某物，尤指时间或注意力
senses.example: Could you afford me a few minutes before the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 开会前能给我几分钟吗？
senses.why: This is the 'give out, spare' branch at its most personal: what is granted is not money or goods but a slice of someone's time.
senses.whyCN: 这是「拿得出、让得出」这条线最贴近人的用法：让出的不是钱或物，而是某人的几分钟时间，所以带上客气口气。

intro.en: Afford is a native English word whose oldest recorded shape already meant 'to carry something through'.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本族词，最早的记录形式已经带有「把事情办成」的意思。

items.en: Forth was an adverb meaning 'forward, onward', and it supplied the direction inside the verb.
items.cn: forth 是表示「向前、往外」的副词，为动词提供了向前的方向感。

items.en: Ge- plus forthian formed geforthian, 'to further, promote, accomplish, manage to do'. The prefix ge- marked a completed action.
items.cn: ge- 加 forthian 构成 geforthian，意为「推进、促成、完成、办得到」；前缀 ge- 表示动作完成。

items.en: The word lost its prefix and became aforthen, 'to manage, be able to, provide'. The spelling with aff- appears later.
items.cn: 这个词丢掉前缀，变成 aforthen，意为「办得到、能够、提供」；带 aff- 的拼写出现得更晚。

items.en: The sense 'to be able to pay for' is recorded from the late fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 「付得起」这一义项大约自十四世纪晚期有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word splits into three living branches: money, time and risk; the old 'provide' sense survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语里它分成三条活用的线：钱、时间与风险；古老的「提供」义主要保留在正式书面语中。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the old forth root and the words built from afford with ordinary suffixes; the near-meaning group holds verbs about sparing, giving and carrying.
note.cn: 形近组收古老的 forth 词根，以及由 afford 加普通后缀构成的词；近义组收表示腾出、给予与承担的动词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning forward or onward; the old root that gave afford its forward push.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向前、往外」，是与 afford 同源的古老词根，给动词一股向前的推力。

entries.definition: Cheap enough that ordinary people can pay for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的、价格合理的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being cheap enough for people to pay for.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性、支付能力」，由 affordable 加后缀 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: A term in design and psychology for what an object quietly allows a user to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可供性」，是设计学与心理学术语，指物品本身提示的用法，由本词加后缀 -ance 构成。

entries.definition: To succeed in doing something difficult, often with little to spare; close to the time sense of afford.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法做到」，常暗示余力不多，与 afford 表示「抽得出时间」的用法相近。

entries.definition: To give or set aside time, money or room for someone; the sense behind the polite question can you afford me a minute.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腾出、让出」时间、钱或空间，正是「能给我一分钟吗」这类客气问法背后的意思。

entries.definition: To give or make something available; the nearest match for the sense in afford a view.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提供、给予」，与 afford a view 这类用法最接近。

entries.definition: To accept and carry a cost or burden; close to the risk sense of afford.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、承受」，与 afford 表示「承受后果」的义项接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root geforthian and the frames the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词根 geforthian，以及这个词实际出现的句式。

normal.en: Geforthian is 'to carry a thing through': affording something is managing to carry its cost.
normal.cn: geforthian 是「把事情办成」：afford 一样东西，就是勉强扛得住它的代价。

normal.en: The root forth means forward, so the word always pushes toward a result rather than simply owning.
normal.cn: 词根 forth 是「向前」，所以这个词始终朝着「办成」推，而不只是「拥有」。

normal.en: Affordable, affordability and unaffordable all keep the 'can pay' sense.
normal.cn: affordable、affordability、unaffordable 都保留了「付得起」这层意思。

normal.en: Cannot afford to is the frame for risk: what you cannot afford is a loss, not a thing.
normal.cn: cannot afford to 是谈风险的句式：承受不起的是损失，而不是某样东西。

normal.en: The formal afford a view or afford an opportunity keeps the old sense of giving.
normal.cn: 正式的 afford a view、afford an opportunity 保留了「给予」的老意思。

abstract.en: Picture a hand in a pocket, counting coins before saying yes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进口袋，先数清硬币再点头。

abstract.en: The same hand can hold hours instead of coins, because time is spent the same way.
abstract.cn: 同一只手握的也可以是小时而不是硬币，因为时间也这样被花出去。

abstract.en: Sometimes the hand gives instead of pays, and the word quietly turns into 'provide'.
abstract.cn: 有时这只手不是在付，而是在给，词义就悄悄转成了「提供」。

examples.en: At today's prices, few families can afford a house in that district.
examples.cn: 按现在的价格，那个区没有几户人家买得起房子。

examples.en: I can't afford to waste another morning on this.
examples.cn: 我耗不起再一个上午在这件事上。

examples.en: The wide windows afford a clear view of the bay.
examples.cn: 宽大的窗户让人可以清楚地看到海湾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福德」——伸手摸口袋，福德还够不够：负担得起；也指拿得出、给得起。

root: 古英语 geforthian「推进、实现、办成」，由前缀 ge- 加 forthian「向前」构成，forthian 又与 forth「向前」同源；中古英语作 aforthen，义为「办得到、拿得出」，再从「拿得出」引申出付得起钱、抽得出时间与提供之义。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses come from one gesture: reaching into what you have and finding enough to give out, whether the resource is money, time, strength or a view.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都出自同一个动作：伸手去摸自己所有的，看够不够拿出来——资源可以是钱、时间、力气，也可以是一处景色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches into a pocket and weighs whether there is enough to give out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸进口袋，掂量还拿不拿得出这一份。

branches.en: MONEY: the resource is coins, and the question is whether the price can be met.
branches.cn: 钱线：资源是硬币，问题是这个价钱付不付得起。

branches.en: TIME: the same act of giving out, with hours standing in for coins.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一个「拿得出」的动作，只是把硬币换成小时。

branches.en: RISK: a loss is a burden, and bearing it needs a strength the word tests in the negative.
branches.cn: 风险线：损失是一副担子，扛不扛得住常在否定式里被检验。

branches.en: PROVISION: a thing puts something within reach, and the old 'further' sense returns.
branches.cn: 提供线：某样东西把条件送到你手边，古老的「促成」义在这里回归。

branches.en: PERSON: what is granted is not goods but a piece of someone's time, spoken politely.
branches.cn: 人物线：让出的不是货物，而是某人的一段时间，语气也随之客气。

intro.en: Afford is built from Old English pieces, and modern English then adds ordinary suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: afford 由古英语成分构成，现代英语再用普通后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin cognate, so the Latin column stays empty; every element is recorded in Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语同源词，所以拉丁语一栏留空；每个构词成分在古英语中都有记录。

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；不敢的；恐怕（委婉）；恐怕如此／恐怕不行
definition_en: frightened of something, worried about someone, unwilling to act, or used politely to announce unwelcome news
core_image: 听见声响先往后缩半步，身体比脑子先做出反应
scene: 深夜的走廊里灯光忽明忽暗，孩子停在门口不肯往前走。The little boy is afraid of the dark corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 afraid 是「害怕」（第 1 个义项：对某物感到恐惧）；句意为小男孩怕那条漆黑的走廊。画面里可辨认的是走廊、忽明忽暗的灯与半开的门。

pos.zh: 形容词：害怕的；担心的；不敢的；恐怕（用于委婉告知）

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「无所畏惧的；不害怕的」
同族的基础名词，由古法语动词直接借入，义为「斗殴；骚乱」，afraid 正是其过去分词

senses.title: Frightened of something
senses.definition: feeling fear because something or someone may hurt you
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人或某物可能伤害自己而感到恐惧
senses.example: The child is afraid of the dog next door.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子怕隔壁家的狗。
senses.why: Afraid is the worn-down past participle of affray, 'to disturb, alarm', so it names a state of being alarmed rather than an action.
senses.whyCN: afraid 是 affray「使惊慌」磨平后的过去分词，所以它天生表示「被惊到」的状态，而不是动作。

senses.title: Worried about someone
senses.definition: feeling anxious about what may happen to someone or something you care about
senses.definitionCN: 对在意的某人或某物可能遭遇的事情感到不安
senses.example: She was afraid for her father, who had gone out in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 她很为父亲担心，他在暴风雨里出了门。
senses.why: To be alarmed is also to be unsettled about a harm that has not happened yet, and that unease can point at another person.
senses.whyCN: 被惊到也意味着对尚未发生的伤害放心不下；当这种不安指向另一个人，afraid 就表示「替某人担心」。

senses.title: Unwilling to do something
senses.definition: unwilling to do something because you expect a bad result or feel shy
senses.definitionCN: 因为预料结果不好或觉得不好意思而不愿做某事
senses.example: He was afraid to ask the teacher for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他不敢向老师求助。
senses.why: Fear arrives before the action and stops it, so the participle describes a person held back rather than a danger faced.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧先于动作出现，并把它拦在门口，所以这种用法描述的是被吓退、不敢动手的人，而不是正在面对的危险。

senses.title: I'm afraid: polite regret
senses.definition: used in the phrase I'm afraid to tell someone politely that something bad or unwelcome is true
senses.definitionCN: 用于 I'm afraid 这一说法，客气地告诉对方某个坏消息或不顺心的事是真的
senses.example: I'm afraid the last train has already left.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕末班车已经开走了。
senses.why: English softens bad news by naming an inner alarm first: the speaker reports a fear rather than a fact, and the hearer takes the point.
senses.whyCN: 英语先说心里的不安，再让坏消息落地：说话人报告的是「我怕」，而不是「事实是」，听者自然领会，语气就被缓冲了。

senses.title: I'm afraid so or not
senses.definition: used in short answers such as I'm afraid so or I'm afraid not to agree reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 I'm afraid so 或 I'm afraid not 这类简短回答，表示勉强同意或否定
senses.example: Will it rain tomorrow? I'm afraid so.
senses.exampleCN: 明天会下雨吗？恐怕会。
senses.why: The same polite alarm is compressed into a two-word reply, so a reluctant answer needs no further explanation.
senses.whyCN: 同一种客气的「不安」被压成两个词的应答，于是勉强的回答不必再解释，听者也知道说话人并不情愿。

intro.en: Afraid is a past participle that became an adjective, and its source verb crossed Frankish, Vulgar Latin and Old French before reaching English.
intro.cn: afraid 是一个变成形容词的过去分词，其来源动词先后经过法兰克语、俗拉丁语与古法语，最后进入英语。

items.en: *Frithu is the reconstructed Frankish word for 'peace', related to German Friede. The asterisk marks a form not directly recorded.
items.cn: *frithu 是重构的法兰克语「和平」一词，与德语 Friede 相关；星号表示这一形式没有直接文献记录。

items.en: Ex- 'out of' plus *fridu 'peace' gave a reconstructed verb *exfridare, 'to put someone out of peace, disturb'.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 *fridu「和平」，构成重构动词 *exfridare，意为「使人失去安宁、扰乱」。

items.en: Old French esfreer meant 'to disturb, frighten, alarm', and its noun esfrei gave English affray.
items.cn: 古法语 esfreer 意为「扰乱、使惊恐」，其名词 esfrei 给出英语的 affray。

items.en: The Anglo-French verb afrayer carried the word to England; its past participle afrayed was used as an adjective.
items.cn: 英法语动词 afrayer 把这个词带到英格兰，其过去分词 afrayed 被当作形容词使用。

items.en: The participle afraid became a full adjective, and from the nineteenth century the polite phrase I'm afraid spread as a softener.
items.cn: 分词 afraid 完全变成形容词；十九世纪以后，客气的 I'm afraid 作为缓冲语广泛流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the affray family and old forms easily confused with it; the near-meaning group holds the ordinary words for fear.
note.cn: 形近组收 affray 一族以及容易与之混淆的旧形式；近义组收表示恐惧的常用词。

entries.definition: A noun for a public fight or disturbance; the parent word whose past participle became afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斗殴、骚乱」，正是那个过去分词变成 afraid 的源头名词。

entries.definition: Not frightened; formed from afraid with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不害怕的」，由本词加否定前缀 un- 构成。

entries.definition: An old or dialectal form of afraid, still heard in some regional speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，afraid 的古老或方言形式，义仍为「害怕的」，在部分地区口语中还能听到。

entries.definition: An old verb meaning to frighten; it looks close to afraid but descends from Old English afyrhtan.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使惊恐」，与 afraid 意思相近、拼写也像，但源自古英语 afyrhtan，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Feeling fear; the most neutral everyday word, usable before a noun as afraid is not.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」，是最中性的日常说法，且可以放在名词前，而 afraid 不能这样用。

entries.definition: Frightened, in a more conversational tone than afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的、吓着的」，语气比 afraid 更口语。

entries.definition: Frightened or anxious, in a more literary and formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的、忧惧的」，语气正式，带书面色彩。

entries.definition: Anxious about a possible problem; covers the 'afraid for someone' sense without any physical fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「担心的」，对应 afraid 表示「为某人担心」的义项，但不含身体上的恐惧。

entries.definition: Extremely frightened; much stronger than afraid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极度恐惧的」，程度远强于 afraid。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real route from the verb affray to the adjective afraid, plus the phrases the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子沿着从动词 affray 到形容词 afraid 的真实路径，并配合这个词常用的说法。

normal.en: Affray is the old verb 'to disturb'; afraid is its past participle, a state of being disturbed.
normal.cn: affray 是古动词「使惊慌」，afraid 是它的过去分词，表示「被惊到」的状态。

normal.en: Old French esfreer goes back to a reconstructed phrase meaning 'out of peace'.
normal.cn: 古法语 esfreer 可追到一个重构说法，意思是「失去安宁」。

normal.en: The prefix un- gives unafraid, the direct opposite.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 un- 就得到 unafraid，正好相反。

normal.en: I'm afraid is polite hedging: the speaker reports an inner alarm, not a fact.
normal.cn: I'm afraid 是客气的缓冲：说话人报告的是心里的不安，而不是事实。

normal.en: Afraid to do marks fear before an action, while afraid of marks fear of a thing.
normal.cn: afraid to do 指动作之前的恐惧，afraid of 指对某样东西的恐惧。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping back from a door before touching the handle.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人还没碰到门把手就先退了一步。

abstract.en: The same step back can be shyness, caution or dread, which is why one word covers all three.
abstract.cn: 同样这一退，可以是害羞、谨慎或恐惧，所以一个词能覆盖三种情形。

abstract.en: When the step back is only politeness, the fear shrinks into a phrase for bad news.
abstract.cn: 当这一退只是客气时，恐惧就缩小成一句通报坏消息的话。

examples.en: The child is afraid of the dog next door.
examples.cn: 那孩子怕隔壁家的狗。

examples.en: I'm afraid the last train has already left.
examples.cn: 恐怕末班车已经开走了。

examples.en: He was afraid to ask the teacher for help.
examples.cn: 他不敢向老师求助。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿弗雷德」——听见怪声先缩一下：害怕的；也用「恐怕」来报坏消息。

root: afraid 是古法语 esfreer「使惊慌」的过去分词，esfreer 一般认为出自俗拉丁语重构形式 *exfridare「使失去安宁」，由 ex-「出」加法兰克语 *frithu「和平」构成；其词根属日耳曼语，与拉丁语并无同源关系，拉丁语只留下前缀 ex-。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses grow from one bodily reaction: a start of alarm, which can settle on an object, on a person, on an action, or thin out into pure politeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都从同一个身体反应长出来：一惊，这份惊可以落在东西上、落在人身上、挡在动作前，也可以淡成纯粹的客气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person steps back half a pace before the mind has time to explain why.
core.cn: 核心意象：人先往后缩了半步，脑子还来不及解释原因。

branches.en: THE THING: the alarm fixes on a dog, a height or a dark corridor.
branches.cn: 物件线：这份惊落在一条狗、一处高处或一条黑走廊上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same unease turns outward and watches over someone else.
branches.cn: 人物线：同一种不安转朝外，替另一个人守着。

branches.en: THE ACTION: fear arrives first and holds the hand back.
branches.cn: 动作线：恐惧先到，把手拦在半路。

branches.en: THE APOLOGY: the alarm is named only to soften unwelcome news.
branches.cn: 致歉线：说出这份不安，只是为了把坏消息说软一些。

branches.en: THE REPLY: the whole softening shrinks into two words of reluctant agreement.
branches.cn: 应答线：整套缓冲缩成两个词，表示勉强的同意。

intro.en: Afraid is assembled from a Germanic peace root, a Latin prefix, a French verb and an English participle ending.
intro.cn: afraid 由日耳曼语的「和平」词根、拉丁语前缀、法语动词与英语分词词尾一层层拼成。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix ex- is directly recorded in Latin; the verb *exfridare is a reconstructed Vulgar Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中只有前缀 ex- 有直接记录，动词 *exfridare 属于重构的俗拉丁语形式。

items.example: It opens the Vulgar Latin verb behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 它开启了这个词背后的俗拉丁语动词。

items.example: The reconstructed form is the peace that fear takes away.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构形式就是恐惧所夺走的「安宁」。

items.meaning: to put out of peace, disturb
items.example: The reconstructed verb joins the prefix and the peace root.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构动词把前缀和「安宁」词根合在一起。

items.example: Old French kept the prefix in esfreer.
items.exampleCN: 古法语在 esfreer 中保留了这个前缀。

items.example: The stem supplies the participle afrayed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干给出分词 afrayed。

items.meaning: the state resulting from an action
items.example: It turned afrayed into the adjective afraid.
items.exampleCN: 它把 afrayed 变成形容词 afraid。

items.example: It forms unafraid.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unafraid。

items.example: The noun is the participle stripped of its ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是去掉词尾的那个分词。

latinEntries.meaning: to put out of peace, disturb

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 un- 加本词构成，义为「无所畏惧的」
同族基础名词，由古法语 esfrei 直接借入，义为「斗殴；骚乱」

definition_zh: 在……之后（时间）；在……之后（顺序、位置）；追赶；仿照、以……命名；问候、打听；之后（副词）；毕竟
definition_en: later than something in time, following it in order or place, in pursuit of it, in imitation of it, or in the fixed phrase after all
core_image: 一个人走在另一人的后面，踩着同一串脚印往前
scene: 散场的人群从剧场门口涌出，台阶上还留着刚才的雨。We went for noodles after the play.
sceneCN: 这里 after 是「在……之后」（第 1 个义项：时间上晚于某事）；句意为看完戏之后我们去吃了面。画面里可辨认的是剧场出口、湿台阶与散场的人群。

pos.zh: 介词：在……之后；追赶；仿照；问候
副词：以后；之后
连词：在……之后

collocations.zh: 问候某人；打听某人的近况

forms.label: 无屈折变化（介词、副词、连词）

derivatives.zh: 由 afterward 加副词属格词尾 -s 构成，义为「之后；后来」
由 after 加古英语 mæth「一次割草」复合而成，义为「后果；余波」
由 after 加 thought 复合而成，义为「事后想到的补充；事后聪明」

senses.title: Later than a time
senses.definition: later in time than an event, hour or date
senses.definitionCN: 在某个事件、钟点或日期之后的时间上
senses.example: We went for a walk after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后我们去散了步。
senses.why: Old English æfter meant 'behind, following': the earlier thing stands in front and the later one stands at its back.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 æfter 本义是「在后面、跟随」，先发生的事站在前头，后发生的事落在它背后，时间上的「之后」就是这个空间图像的转用。

senses.title: Following in order or place
senses.definition: following something in a series, an order or a position
senses.definitionCN: 在一个序列、次序或位置中跟在某物之后
senses.example: Turn left after the second bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 过了第二座桥后向左转。
senses.why: The spatial 'behind' is the oldest layer: one thing passes, and another comes behind it along the same road.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「在后面」是最早的一层意思：一件东西过去，另一件沿着同一条路跟在它后面，所以顺序义直接沿用这个图像。

senses.title: In pursuit of
senses.definition: following someone or something in order to catch it or get it
senses.definitionCN: 跟在某人或某物后面，为的是抓住它或得到它
senses.example: The dog ran after the ball across the lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 狗穿过草坪去追那只球。
senses.why: To stay behind a moving thing is also to chase it, because whatever remains behind keeps the same direction.
senses.whyCN: 落在移动的东西后面，也就是在追它，因为一直待在后面的人始终朝着同一个方向走，目标因此变成猎物。

senses.title: In imitation or honour of
senses.definition: using the name or style of someone or something as a model
senses.definitionCN: 以某人或某物的名字、风格作为样板来使用
senses.example: They named the library after a local teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以当地一位教师的姓氏命名了这座图书馆。
senses.why: The one who is followed sets the line, so naming after a person means walking in that person's track.
senses.whyCN: 被跟随的人先定下路线，所以用某人的名字命名，就是沿着那人的足迹走，after 因此带上「仿照」的意思。

senses.title: In search of news about
senses.definition: used in ask after, meaning to ask for news about someone's health or situation
senses.definitionCN: 用于 ask after，表示为某人的健康或近况打听消息
senses.example: My mother asked after you when I called her.
senses.exampleCN: 我给母亲打电话时，她问起了你的近况。
senses.why: The question follows the absent person and goes looking for him, so the 'behind' image becomes concern that tracks someone down.
senses.whyCN: 询问追着不在场的人跑，去找他的消息，于是「跟在后面」变成了关切地打听，话虽轻，方向仍是朝着那个人。

senses.title: Following the time when
senses.definition: used as a conjunction to introduce an event that happens later than another
senses.definitionCN: 作连词使用，引出比另一件事发生得更晚的事件
senses.example: After the rain stopped, we set off again.
senses.exampleCN: 雨停之后，我们又出发了。
senses.why: The preposition grew a clause: now a whole event, not just a noun, can stand in front of the follower.
senses.whyCN: 介词长出了从句用法：不再只接一个名词，整个事件都能站到「跟随者」前面，由 after 引出整句话。

senses.title: Later, afterwards
senses.definition: later in time, used as an adverb with nothing following it
senses.definitionCN: 时间上较晚，作副词使用，后面不接宾语
senses.example: She arrived at nine and left soon after.
senses.exampleCN: 她九点到，不久之后就走了。
senses.why: With nothing to follow in the sentence, the word keeps only the bare idea of 'later'.
senses.whyCN: 句子里没有可跟的对象时，这个词只剩下「后来」这一层最单纯的意思，所以能单独站在句尾。

senses.title: After all
senses.definition: used in the phrase after all to mean in spite of everything, or for a reason just remembered
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 after all，表示尽管有种种情况，或表示想到了某个才记起的理由
senses.example: Don't be too hard on him; he is only a child after all.
senses.exampleCN: 别对他太严厉，他毕竟只是个孩子。
senses.why: The phrase means 'after everything has been counted', and what follows the counting is the final judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的字面是「把一切数完之后」，数完之后的结论就是最后的判断，所以引申为「毕竟、终究」。

intro.en: After is a Germanic word with a comparative shape, and its spatial meaning widened into time, order, pursuit and imitation.
intro.cn: after 是带比较级形态的日耳曼语词，它的空间义逐步扩展到时间、顺序、追赶与仿照。

items.en: *Apo is the reconstructed root meaning 'away, off', and its comparative *apotero- meant 'further away'.
items.cn: *apo 是重构词根，意为「离开、向外」，其比较级 *apotero- 表示「更远、更靠后」。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic adverb *after meant 'further behind, later', built on the same comparative idea.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语副词 *after 意为「更靠后、更晚」，建立在同一个比较级概念上。

items.en: Æfter meant 'behind, following, later, in pursuit of', covering place and time from the beginning.
items.cn: æfter 意为「在后面、跟随、后来、追赶」，从一开始就同时覆盖空间与时间。

items.en: The word extended to 'in imitation of, in honour of' and to 'in search of news', as in named after and ask after.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到「仿照、为纪念」以及「打听消息」，于是有了 named after 与 ask after 的用法。

items.en: After works as preposition, adverb and conjunction, and it also builds compounds such as afternoon and afterwards.
items.cn: 现代英语里 after 可作介词、副词与连词，还构成 afternoon、afterwards 这类复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds compounds and derivatives built on after; the near-meaning group holds words for what follows in space, order or time.
note.cn: 形近组收以 after 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示在空间、顺序或时间上随后的词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning later or after that, built from afterward with an adverbial ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后、后来」，由 afterward 加副词词尾构成，与 after 同源。

entries.definition: The situation that follows a serious event; literally a second mowing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果、余波」，字面是「第二次割草」，与 after 同源复合。

entries.definition: A formal adverb meaning after that time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此后、在那之后」，语气正式，与 after 同源。

entries.definition: The part of the day following noon; a compound of after and noon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下午」，由 after 与 noon 复合而成，与 after 同源。

entries.definition: At the back of something; purely spatial, with no idea of time.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……后面」，纯指空间，不含时间义。

entries.definition: Coming after something in order; often a little more formal than after.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或形容词，义为「在……之后、接着的」，多用于次序，语气比 after 稍正式。

entries.definition: At a time in the future or after the moment being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来、稍后」，只谈时间，不涉及顺序或追赶。

entries.definition: Coming after something else in time; an adjective used in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「随后的、接下来的」，用于正式书面语，只能作定语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English æfter and the set phrases the word forms today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 æfter，以及这个词今天构成的固定说法。

normal.en: Old English æfter meant 'behind': the later event stands at the back of the earlier one.
normal.cn: 古英语 æfter 意为「在后面」：后发生的事站在先发生的事背后。

normal.en: The same word covers place, order and time, because all three can be lined up front to back.
normal.cn: 同一个词能管空间、顺序与时间，因为这三者都能从前往后排成一线。

normal.en: To run after something is to stay behind it while it moves.
normal.cn: run after 某物，就是在它移动时一直跟在后面。

normal.en: Naming after someone means walking in that person's track.
normal.cn: 以某人的名字命名，就是沿着那人的足迹走。

normal.en: After all means 'after everything has been counted', hence 'in spite of everything'.
normal.cn: after all 的字面是「把一切数完之后」，所以引申为「毕竟」。

abstract.en: Picture a row of footprints, each one just behind the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一串脚印，每一个都紧挨在前一个后面。

abstract.en: The footprints can be laid on a road, on a shelf or on a calendar without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 这串脚印可以铺在路上、摆在书架上或印在日历上，形状始终不变。

abstract.en: Whatever stands behind another thing is 'after' it, even when nothing is moving at all.
abstract.cn: 凡是站在另一件东西后面的，都算在它「之后」，即使没有任何东西在移动。

examples.en: We sat by the river long after the sun had set.
examples.cn: 太阳落山很久以后，我们还坐在河边。

examples.en: The dog ran after the ball across the lawn.
examples.cn: 狗穿过草坪去追那只球。

examples.en: They named the library after a local teacher.
examples.cn: 他们以当地一位教师的姓氏命名了这座图书馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿福特」——总有一双鞋跟在后头：在……之后；也指追赶、仿照。

root: 古英语 æfter「在后面、跟随、后来」来自原始日耳曼语重构形式 *after，更早可追到原始印欧语 *apo「离开」的比较级 *apotero-「更靠后」；空间上的「在后」后来扩展到时间、顺序、追赶与仿照。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of after follows one picture: something moves or stands at the back of something else, and the back position is read as time, order, pursuit, imitation or concern.
sensesIntro.cn: after 的每个义项都沿着同一个画面：某物跟或站在另一物的后面，而这个「后面的位置」被读成时间、顺序、追赶、仿照或关切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller walks one step behind another, stepping into the same prints.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人落后一步，踩着前一个人的同一串脚印往前走。

branches.en: TIME: the back position is read on a clock, in a clause, or as a bare adverb.
branches.cn: 时间线：把「在后面」读在钟点上、读进从句里，或读成单独的副词。

branches.en: ORDER AND PLACE: the same line is read along a road, a queue or a list.
branches.cn: 顺序线：同一条线被读在路上、队伍里或一份名单上。

branches.en: PURSUIT: to stay behind a moving thing is to chase it.
branches.cn: 追赶线：一直跟在移动的东西后面，就是在追它。

branches.en: MODEL: the person who is followed sets the line for a name or a style.
branches.cn: 仿照线：被跟随的人为名字或风格定下路线。

branches.en: CONCERN AND JUDGEMENT: following an absent person becomes asking after him, and counting everything first becomes after all.
branches.cn: 关切与判断线：跟着不在场的人变成问候，把一切先数完则变成「毕竟」。

intro.en: After is a Germanic root plus old suffixes; the modern language keeps it as a free word and as a combining form.
intro.cn: after 是日耳曼语词根加古老后缀，现代英语既把它当独立的词，也把它当前缀性的复合成分。

latinIntro.en: After has no Latin cognate, so this column is empty; the chain runs through Germanic and reconstructed Indo-European forms only.
latinIntro.cn: after 没有拉丁语同源词，所以这一栏留空；词源链只在日耳曼语与印欧语重构形式之间展开。

items.example: The Old English form already carried both place and time.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语形式已经同时带空间与时间两层意思。

items.example: The reconstructed form is a comparative of 'away'.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构形式是「离开」一词的比较级。

items.example: The root is the starting point of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是整族词的起点。

items.example: It forms æfterweard, the ancestor of afterward.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 æfterweard，即 afterward 的前身。

items.example: It builds compounds such as afternoon and aftermath.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 afternoon、aftermath 这类复合词。

items.example: It forms afterward.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 afterward。

items.meaning: marks an adverb of time or direction
items.meaningCN: 构成表时间或方向的副词
items.example: It forms afterwards and towards.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 afterwards 与 towards。

items.example: It appears in aftermath, originally a second crop.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 aftermath 中，原指第二次割下的草。

derivatives.zh: 由 afterward 加副词属格词尾 -s 构成，义为「之后；后来」
由 after 加古英语 mæth「一次割草」复合而成，义为「后果；余波」
由 after 加 thought 复合而成，义为「事后想到的补充」

definition_zh: 下午；午后；下午的（定语）；午后的一段时间；下午场；人生的后半段
definition_en: the part of the day between noon and the evening, or an attributive word for things happening then
core_image: 日头刚过正中最高的位置，开始斜斜地往下走
scene: 窗外的光斜斜照进来，茶杯在桌上留下一道长长的影子。She likes to read in the afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 afternoon 是「下午」（第 1 个义项：正午到傍晚之间的时段）；句意为她喜欢在下午读书。画面里可辨认的是斜光、茶杯与窗台。

pos.zh: 名词：下午；午后的一段时间；下午场
形容词（定语）：下午的
副词（复数形式）：每天下午

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 mid- 加本词构成，义为「下午中段；午后三四点前后」
由本词的复数形式固定为副词，义为「每天下午」

senses.title: The part of the day after noon
senses.definition: the period of the day between noon and the evening
senses.definitionCN: 正午与傍晚之间的那段时间
senses.example: The afternoon was hot and the streets were empty.
senses.exampleCN: 那个下午很热，街上空荡荡的。
senses.why: The word is a compound of after and noon, so it simply names the stretch that follows the middle of the day.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 after 加 noon 的复合，字面意思是「正午之后」，于是直接命名正午到傍晚之间的那段时间。

senses.title: Of the afternoon
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean happening in or belonging to the afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示发生在下午或属于下午
senses.example: The afternoon light made the kitchen look warm.
senses.exampleCN: 午后的光让厨房显得很温暖。
senses.why: English lets a time noun stand in front of another noun as a label, so afternoon becomes an adjective without any ending.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时间名词直接放在另一个名词前面充当标签，所以 afternoon 不必加任何词尾就能当定语用。

senses.title: A period spent in a certain way
senses.definition: a particular stretch of the afternoon, especially one spent on an activity
senses.definitionCN: 下午中特定的一段，尤指花在某项活动上的一段时间
senses.example: We spent the whole afternoon cleaning the garage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们整个下午都在打扫车库。
senses.why: Once the word names a block of time, it can be counted like a container: an afternoon can be filled.
senses.whyCN: 一旦它指一段可以划分的时间，就能像容器一样被计数：一个下午可以被某件事填满，于是成了可数的单位。

senses.title: An afternoon performance
senses.definition: a performance or showing that takes place in the afternoon, especially in a theatre
senses.definitionCN: 在下午举行的演出或放映，尤指剧院里的午后场次
senses.example: They booked tickets for the Saturday afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们订了星期六下午场的票。
senses.why: In the theatre the time slot itself becomes the name of the show, so an afternoon is a matinee.
senses.whyCN: 在剧院里，时间段本身成了演出的名称，所以「下午」就指午后那一场演出，无需另造新词。

senses.title: The later part of life
senses.definition: used in literature for the later part of a person's life, pictured as the afternoon of that life
senses.definitionCN: 文学用语，指一个人生命的后半段，把它想象成这一天的下午
senses.example: In the afternoon of his life he returned to the village he had left.
senses.exampleCN: 在人生的后半段，他回到了当年离开的村庄。
senses.why: A day runs from morning to evening, and a life is pictured the same way, so its second half becomes an afternoon.
senses.whyCN: 一天从早晨走到傍晚，人生也照此想象，于是生命走过正午之后的那一半就成了「下午」。

senses.title: Every afternoon
senses.definition: used in the plural form afternoons as an adverb meaning on every afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 用复数形式 afternoons 作副词，表示在每个下午
senses.example: He practises the violin at the old hall afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天下午都在旧礼堂里练小提琴。
senses.why: American English turns the plural into an adverb of repeated time, the same way mornings and evenings work.
senses.whyCN: 美式英语把复数形式直接用作副词，表示反复发生的时间，与 mornings、evenings 的做法一致。

intro.en: Afternoon is an English compound, but its second half, noon, came from a Latin phrase for the ninth hour of the day.
intro.cn: afternoon 是英语复合词，但它的后半部分 noon 源自拉丁语表示「第九时」的说法。

items.en: Nona hora meant 'the ninth hour' after sunrise, roughly the middle of the afternoon in Roman reckoning.
items.cn: nona hora 意为日出后的「第九时」，按罗马人的计时大约落在下午中段。

items.en: The church borrowed the Latin hour and English kept it as non, still naming the ninth hour.
items.cn: 教会借用了这个拉丁钟点，英语保留为 non，仍指白天的第九时。

items.en: The meaning of noon moved from mid-afternoon to twelve o'clock, and the old word for midday was pushed aside.
items.cn: noon 的词义从下午中段移到正午十二点，原先表示正午的旧词被它取代。

items.en: After and noon were joined to name the hours that follow midday; the written form was at first two words.
items.cn: after 与 noon 连用，命名正午之后的那几个小时；起初写作两个词。

items.en: The compound settled into one word, and it grew attributive and theatrical uses such as afternoon tea and the Saturday afternoon.
items.cn: 这个复合词固定为一个词，并发展出定语与剧场用法，如 afternoon tea 与星期六下午场。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the noon element and words built around it; the near-meaning group holds the other parts of the day.
note.cn: 形近组收 noon 这个成分以及围绕它构成的词；近义组收一天中的其它时段。

entries.definition: Twelve o'clock in the day; the second half of the compound afternoon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午、中午」，是复合词 afternoon 的后半部分，二者同源。

entries.definition: The middle of the afternoon, around three or four o'clock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下午中段」，大约在午后三四点，由前缀 mid- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A literary word for noon, or the time around it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午、午时」，是 noon 的文学化说法，与本词共享同一成分。

entries.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock; a point rather than a stretch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午」，指一天的中点，是一个时间点而不是一段时光。

entries.definition: The part of the day between the afternoon and night.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「傍晚、晚上」，是下午之后、夜晚之前的那一段。

entries.definition: The part of the day from sunrise until noon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上午、早晨」，指日出到正午之间的时段，与下午相对。

entries.definition: The darker stage of twilight, when the day is almost over.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄昏、薄暮」，指一天将尽、光线转暗的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real compound after plus noon and the Latin hour behind noon.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的复合结构 after 加 noon，以及 noon 背后的拉丁语钟点。

normal.en: Afternoon is simply after plus noon: the stretch that follows the middle of the day.
normal.cn: afternoon 就是 after 加 noon：正午之后的那一段。

normal.en: Noon itself comes from Latin nona hora, the ninth hour, which once fell in mid-afternoon.
normal.cn: noon 来自拉丁语 nona hora「第九时」，那个钟点原本就落在下午。

normal.en: English lets a time noun sit before another noun, so afternoon tea needs no ending.
normal.cn: 英语允许时间名词放在另一个名词前，所以 afternoon tea 不必加词尾。

normal.en: Afternoons as an adverb follows the pattern of mornings and evenings.
normal.cn: afternoons 作副词，走的是 mornings、evenings 的路子。

normal.en: The afternoon of life is a literary picture of a person's later years.
normal.cn: the afternoon of life 是对人生后半段的文学化说法。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hand has just passed the top and begins to slide down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针刚越过顶端，开始往下滑。

abstract.en: The light is still strong but already leaning, which is exactly what the word names.
abstract.cn: 光还亮，却已经斜了，这个词命名的正是这个状态。

abstract.en: Any block of that leaning light can be filled, booked or remembered, so it becomes a countable thing.
abstract.cn: 这段斜光可以被填满、被预订、被记住，于是成了一个可以计数的事物。

examples.en: The afternoon was hot and the streets were empty.
examples.cn: 那个下午很热，街上空荡荡的。

examples.en: We spent the whole afternoon cleaning the garage.
examples.cn: 我们整个下午都在打扫车库。

examples.en: He practises the violin at the old hall afternoons.
examples.cn: 他每天下午都在旧礼堂里练小提琴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿夫特努恩」——午饭吃完，日头偏西：下午；午后的一段时光。

root: after 与 noon 的复合词。noon 源自拉丁语 nona hora「第九时」，经教会用语进入古英语作 non，指白天第九个钟点，后来词义移到正午；afternoon 即「正午之后的那段时光」。

sensesIntro.en: All six senses circle one image: the hours just after the sun passes its highest point, which can be a period, a label, a container of activity, a show time or a stage of life.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都围绕同一个画面：太阳越过最高点之后的那几个小时，它可以是一段时光、一个定语、一个装活动的容器、一个演出时段，也可以是人生的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun has just passed the top of its arc and the shadows begin to lengthen.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳刚越过弧线的顶点，影子开始被拉长。

branches.en: THE PERIOD: the hours between noon and evening get a single name.
branches.cn: 时段线：正午到傍晚之间的那几个小时有了一个统一的名字。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the same word stands before a noun and marks when something happens.
branches.cn: 定语线：同一个词站到名词前，标出事情发生的时段。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: a block of time can be filled with one activity.
branches.cn: 容器线：一段可以划分的时间能被一件事填满。

branches.en: THE STAGE: in a theatre the time slot itself becomes the name of a performance.
branches.cn: 场次线：在剧院里，时间段本身成了演出的名称。

branches.en: TWO EXTENSIONS: the same arc is stretched over a whole life, or repeated day after day.
branches.cn: 两端延伸：同一条弧线可以拉长到一生，也可以按天反复出现。

intro.en: Afternoon is a native English compound whose second element carries a Latin history.
intro.cn: afternoon 是英语本族复合词，但它的第二个成分带着一段拉丁语的历史。

latinIntro.en: Nona, hora and the phrase nona hora are all recorded in Latin; Old English non is the borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: nona、hora 以及 nona hora 这一说法在拉丁语中都有记录，古英语 non 是它的借形。

items.example: It names the ninth hour of the Roman day.
items.exampleCN: 它指罗马人白天里的第九个钟点。

items.example: It combines with nona to give nona hora.
items.exampleCN: 它与 nona 合成 nona hora。

items.example: The church borrowed the Latin hour and shortened it.
items.exampleCN: 教会借用这个拉丁钟点，并在英语里把它缩短。

items.example: Noon is the joint of the compound.
items.exampleCN: noon 是这个复合词的接合处。

items.example: It adds the idea of what comes later.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「之后」的意思。

items.example: It forms midafternoon.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 midafternoon。

items.example: It carries the noon meaning inside compounds.
items.exampleCN: 它在复合词内部承载「正午」的意思。

items.example: It forms afternoons, used as an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 afternoons，并用作副词。
