definition_zh: 以前；……之前；很久以前；方才
definition_en: before the present time, used after a period of time to show how far back something happened
core_image: 从此刻往回量出一段距离，把事件钉在那段距离的末端
scene: 老相册摊在木桌上，摊主指着一张泛黄的合影，说那是很久以前拍的。That photograph was taken more than thirty years ago.
sceneCN: 这里 ago 表示「距今……以前」（第 1 个义项：从现在往回数一段时间）；句意为那张照片拍摄于三十多年前。木桌、相册与泛黄的合影构成画面。

pos.zh: 副词：以前、……之前，放在表示时长的词组之后

derivatives.zh: 古旧的同义形式，义为「以前」；它并非由本词加后缀派生，而是同一个词在早期英语里的另一种写法
由 by 与 gone 构成的复合词，gone 与 ago 的后半部分同出古英语 gān「走」，义为「过去的、往昔的」

senses.title: A span measured back from now
senses.definition: used after a word or phrase for a length of time to say how far in the past something happened, counted from now
senses.definitionCN: 用在表示时长的词或词组之后，表示某事发生在从此刻往回数的那段距离之前
senses.example: She moved to this city eight years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她八年前搬到了这座城市。
senses.why: The word began as a past participle meaning 'gone by', so a span placed before it is a stretch of time that has already gone past the speaker.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本是意为「已经走过去」的过去分词，所以放在它前面的时段，就是从说话人此刻已经走过去的那段距离，事件则停在那段距离的末端。

senses.title: At a distant, unmeasured time
senses.definition: in the phrases long ago or a long time ago, at a time so distant that the exact distance does not matter
senses.definitionCN: 用于 long ago 或 a long time ago，指遥远得不必计量具体距离的过去
senses.example: Long ago, people told the time by the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，人们靠太阳判断时间。
senses.why: When the speaker does not count the span, the same backward measure becomes a vague horizon instead of a number.
senses.whyCN: 当说话人不数具体长度时，同一个朝回量的动作就失去了刻度，变成一条模糊的地平线，于是有了「很久以前」这种不计量距离的说法。

senses.title: In questions about distance in time
senses.definition: in questions with how long, asking the distance in time between now and a past event
senses.definitionCN: 在 how long 引导的疑问句中，询问此刻与过去某事相隔多长时间
senses.example: How long ago did you last see her?
senses.exampleCN: 你上次见到她是多久以前？
senses.why: The measuring word becomes a question word: the same ruler is still held up, but the speaker now asks for its reading.
senses.whyCN: 量尺还在手里，只是换成了疑问口吻：说话人不再报出刻度，而是请对方读出此刻到那件事之间有多长。

senses.title: Only a short while back
senses.definition: in phrases such as a moment ago or a minute ago, marking a very short distance back from now
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a moment ago、a minute ago 等说法，标记与此刻相隔极短的过去
senses.example: He left the office a minute ago.
senses.exampleCN: 他一分钟前刚离开办公室。
senses.why: Shrink the span to its smallest and the word stops measuring history; it marks only what has just slipped past.
senses.whyCN: 把时段缩到极小，这个词就不再丈量历史，只用来标出刚刚滑过去的那一下，所以中文对译成「刚才」最贴切。

senses.title: Before a past reference point
senses.titleCN: 以过去某刻为参照的以前
senses.definition: in reported speech, used after a span when the point of reference is a past moment rather than the moment of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 在转述句中，参照点是过去某一时刻而非说话此刻时，仍用这个词表示相隔多久
senses.example: He told me that the letter had arrived two weeks ago.
senses.exampleCN: 他告诉我那封信两周前就到了。
senses.why: The measure is taken from whichever moment the speaker is standing in; when the whole scene is shifted into the past, the ruler moves with it, and some grammars prefer before in this position.
senses.whyCN: 这把尺子量的是「说话人所站的那一刻」到事件的距离；整个场景被移入过去时，尺子也跟着移过去，因此有了这种转述用法，而部分语法书在此位置更主张用 before。

intro.en: Ago is a native English word, not a Latin loan; it began as the past participle of an Old English verb meaning 'to go by, pass'.
intro.cn: ago 是英语本族词，并非拉丁语借词；它原本是一个意为「走过去、逝去」的古英语动词的过去分词。

items.en: Gān meant 'to go' and belonged to a strong verb class; its past participle had the same shape as the infinitive, also written gān.
items.cn: gān 意为「走」，属强变化动词；它的过去分词与动词原形同形，也写作 gān。

items.en: The prefix ā- 'away, forth' plus gān made āgān, 'to go by, pass away'. The verb is often transliterated as agan in later handbooks.
items.cn: 前缀 ā-「离开、向前」加 gān 构成 āgān，意为「走过去、逝去」；后世手册常把它转写为 agan。

items.en: The participle form of this verb, written āgen or agon, supplied the later adverb; whether it should be linked with the separate verb āgan 'to own' is disputed, so that detail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词的分词形式写作 āgen 或 agon，后来的副词即由此而来；它是否应与另一个表示「拥有」的动词 āgan 联系起来，各家说法不一，这一点来源不确定。

items.en: In Middle English the form ago or agon settled after a phrase of time, as in 'three days ago', and stopped behaving like a participle.
items.cn: 中古英语中，ago 或 agon 固定出现在表示时间的词组之后，如「三天以前」，不再像分词那样使用。

items.en: Since the sixteenth century the word has been a fixed backward marker: it measures from the speaker's present and never stands before the span.
items.cn: 十六世纪以后，这个词成了一个固定的「往回指」标记：只以说话人的此刻为起点，并且从不放在时段之前。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms built on the Old English verb gān 'to go' together with words that merely resemble ago; the near-meaning group holds other ways of pointing backwards in time.
note.cn: 形近组收由古英语动词 gān「走」构成的形式，以及只是外形相近的词；近义组收其他指向过去的时间说法。

entries.definition: An archaic form of ago, also meaning gone by or past.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧形式，与 ago 同义，义为「以前、已往」，今只见于旧诗文。

entries.definition: The modern verb meaning to move or travel; its Old English ancestor gān is the second element inside ago.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「走、去」；其古英语前身 gān 正是 ago 的后半部分，两者同源。

entries.definition: Very eager or excited; it only looks like ago and comes from Old French.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「急切期待的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自古法语。

entries.definition: The self or a person's sense of self-worth; a Latin pronoun with no link to ago.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自我、自尊」；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同，来自拉丁语代词。

entries.definition: At an earlier time; it can stand alone, while ago must follow a length of time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以前、在……之前」，可以单独使用，而 ago 必须跟在表示时长的词组后面。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, used mainly in writing and often without any stated span.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「先前、此前」，多用于书面语，通常不交代具体相隔多久。

entries.definition: Before the present or before a mentioned point; it needs no measured span.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「较早、先前」，不需要一个量出来的时段。

entries.definition: Informal, as in three years back; the same backward counting with a looser tone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，口语用法，如 three years back，同样是从现在往回数，语气更随意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English verb gān, the fixed word order of the word, and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语动词 gān、这个词固定的语序，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ago was once a participle meaning 'gone by': the time has already walked past you.
normal.cn: ago 原本是意为「已经走过去」的分词：那段时间已经从你身边走过去了。

normal.en: It always stands after the span: three days ago, never ago three days.
normal.cn: 它永远站在时段后面：three days ago，而不是 ago three days。

normal.en: Long ago drops the number and leaves only a far horizon.
normal.cn: long ago 把数字去掉，只留下远远的一条地平线。

normal.en: How long ago turns the ruler into a question.
normal.cn: how long ago 把这把尺子变成了一句提问。

normal.en: It measures from now, so the verb stays in the past tense.
normal.cn: 它从此刻往回量，所以句子里的动词用过去时。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid backwards from your feet, with the event pinned at the far end.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子从脚下朝后铺开，事件被钉在尺子的另一头。

abstract.en: The longer the span, the fainter the pin; long ago is a pin you can no longer see.
abstract.cn: 时段越长，钉子越模糊；long ago 就是一枚已经看不见的钉子。

abstract.en: A moment ago is the same ruler with almost no length at all.
abstract.cn: a moment ago 是同一把尺子，只是几乎没有长度。

examples.en: She moved to this city eight years ago.
examples.cn: 她八年前搬到了这座城市。

examples.en: Long ago, people told the time by the sun.
examples.cn: 很久以前，人们靠太阳判断时间。

examples.en: He left the office a minute ago.
examples.cn: 他一分钟前刚离开办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额够」——时间已经足够走远，回头一量：以前、在……之前。

root: 古英语 āgān（常转写为 agan）意为「走过去、逝去」，由 ā-「离开、向前」加 gān「走」构成；它的分词形式 āgen 或 agon 演变为副词 ago，因此这个词的核心是「已经走过去了的那段时间」。

sensesIntro.en: All five senses apply the same backward measure from a reference moment; what varies is whether the span is counted, vague, questioned, very short, or shifted into reported past.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都在做同一件事：从某个参照时刻往回量；不同的是那段距离是被数出来、被模糊掉、被拿来做提问、被缩到极短，还是随转述一起被移到过去。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid backwards from the speaker's feet, with a past event pinned somewhere along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子从说话人脚下朝后铺开，过去的事件被钉在尺上某处。

branches.en: THE SPAN: a counted length placed before the word fixes how far back the event lies.
branches.cn: 时段线：放在词前的可数长度，定出事件往回退了多少。

branches.en: THE HORIZON: with long, the scale dissolves and only distance remains.
branches.cn: 地平线：与 long 连用时刻度消失，只剩下遥远。

branches.en: THE QUESTION: the same ruler is held up and the listener is asked to read it.
branches.cn: 提问线：同一把尺子仍举着，只是请听者来读刻度。

branches.en: THE EDGE: shrunk to a moment, the measure marks what has just slipped by.
branches.cn: 边缘线：缩到一个瞬间，量出的就是刚刚滑过去的那一刻。

branches.en: THE SHIFTED SCENE: in reported speech the whole ruler moves back with the story.
branches.cn: 移位线：在转述句中，整把尺子随着故事一起被移到了过去。

intro.en: Ago is built from Old English pieces, and the same pieces still shape the modern go family; English endings are added to those forms, not to ago itself.
intro.cn: ago 由古英语部件构成，这些部件至今仍在塑造现代英语的 go 词族；英语词尾是加在那些形式上，而不是加在 ago 本身。

latinIntro.en: Ago has no Latin relatives: its whole history lies inside Germanic, so the Latin section is left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: ago 没有拉丁语同族词，它的历史全部在日耳曼语内部，因此拉丁同源部分有意留空。

items.example: It marks movement away in verbs such as āgān.
items.exampleCN: 它在 āgān 这类动词中标记「离开」的动作。

items.example: Gān is the verb inside āgān and inside modern go.
items.exampleCN: gān 是 āgān 与现代 go 共有的那个动词。

items.example: It marks the participle form agon.
items.exampleCN: 它标出分词形式 agon。

items.example: It is the modern reflex of gān.
items.exampleCN: 它是 gān 在现代英语里的延续。

items.example: It keeps the old sense of having walked away.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了「已经走开」这一古老含义。

items.example: It pairs by with the old participle of go.
items.exampleCN: 它把 by 与 go 的古老分词组合在一起。

items.example: It shows how productive the go family still is.
items.exampleCN: 它说明 go 这个词族至今仍有构词能力。

items.example: It builds a fresh adjective on going.
items.exampleCN: 它在 going 之上造出一个新的形容词。

definition_zh: 同意；赞成；答应；商定；一致；相符；适合（胃口、体质）
definition_en: to share the same opinion, to say yes to something, to reach a shared decision, or to match and suit
core_image: 两条线从不同方向弯过来，在同一个点上重合
scene: 院墙边的两个邻居争了半天地界，最后都笑了，一起蹲下重新量线。They finally agreed on where the new fence should stand.
sceneCN: 这里 agree 是「商定、达成一致」（第 3 个义项：双方共同决定某事）；句意为他们终于商定了新篱笆该立在哪儿。两人蹲在墙边，气氛由僵持转为缓和。

pos.zh: 动词：同意、赞成；答应；商定；一致、相符；适合

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「协议；同意；一致」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」
由 agreeable 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「愉快地；顺从地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不同意；不一致」
由 disagree 加后缀 -ment 构成，义为「分歧；不一致」

senses.title: To hold the same opinion
senses.definition: to have the same opinion as someone else about something
senses.definitionCN: 在某件事上与别人持有相同的看法
senses.example: I agree with you that the plan needs more time.
senses.exampleCN: 我同意你的看法，这个计划还需要更多时间。
senses.why: Latin ad 'to' plus gratum 'pleasing' meant 'to be pleasing to', hence 'to fall in with'; two minds falling in with each other is simply sharing a view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ad「朝向」加 gratum「合意的」本义是「合对方的心意」，引申为「合到一处」；两个心意能合到一处，就是看法相同。

senses.title: To say yes to a request
senses.definition: to say that you will do what someone has asked or suggested
senses.definitionCN: 表示愿意去做别人请求或建议的事
senses.example: She agreed to lend him the car for the weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应把车借给他用一个周末。
senses.why: The step from liking to consenting is small: what is asked for must first be found agreeable, and the nod is that agreement made audible.
senses.whyCN: 从「合心意」到「点头」只差一步：先觉得对方的请求可以接受，点头就是把这层合意说出口，于是有了「答应」这一义项。

senses.title: To reach a shared decision
senses.definition: to reach a decision or arrangement together after discussion
senses.definitionCN: 经过商议后共同作出决定或安排
senses.example: The two sides agreed on a price after a long night of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一整夜的谈判，双方就价格达成了一致。
senses.why: Here two separate wishes must land on one point at the same time, which is why this sense so often takes on and names the point they chose.
senses.whyCN: 这里要求两份不同的心意同时落到同一个点上；正因为要指出那个共同落点，这个用法常带介词 on，后面跟被接受的具体方案。

senses.title: To match or correspond
senses.definition: of accounts, figures or descriptions, to be the same or to fit together
senses.definitionCN: 指账目、数字或说法彼此相同、能够对得上
senses.example: His story does not agree with the version the witness gave.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与证人的版本对不上。
senses.why: Move the meeting point from people to things: two sets of figures that fit together behave exactly like two minds that have come to terms.
senses.whyCN: 把「合到一处」从人移到物上：两组数字能严丝合缝地对上，就像两个心意谈拢了一样，于是这个词也可以说账目、说法彼此相符。

senses.title: To follow grammatical concord
senses.definition: of a word, to have the same number, person or gender as the word it is grammatically linked to
senses.definitionCN: 指一个词在与它有语法关系的词面前，保持数、人称或性的一致
senses.example: In this sentence the verb must agree with its subject in number.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，动词必须在数上与主语保持一致。
senses.why: Grammar formalises the same fitting together: if the subject is singular, the verb must take the singular shape, or the two ends no longer meet.
senses.whyCN: 语法把这套「彼此相合」形式化了：主语是单数，动词也得取单数形状，两端对不上就算语法错误。

senses.title: To suit the body
senses.definition: of food, drink or a climate, to suit someone and not make them ill
senses.definitionCN: 指食物、饮料或气候适合某人，不让其感到不适
senses.example: Rich food does not agree with me in hot weather.
senses.exampleCN: 天热的时候，油腻的食物不合我的胃口。
senses.why: This is the oldest Latin sense kept almost intact: something that is gratum is pleasing, and food that pleases the body is food that suits it.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义保留得最完整的一支：gratum 就是「令人舒适、合意」，食物与身体相合就叫「合胃口」，不合就让人难受。

intro.en: Agree goes back to Latin gratus 'pleasing' through the Old French verb agreer, and its oldest English sense was 'to please'.
intro.cn: agree 经古法语动词 agreer 上溯到拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」，它在英语里最早的意思是「使满意」。

items.en: Gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome, thankful' and also produced gratia 'grace, favour' and the later gratitude.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、感激的」，还生出 gratia「恩惠、好意」以及后来的 gratitude。

items.en: Ad 'to' plus the neuter form gratum gave the sense 'to be pleasing to, to be in someone's favour'.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加中性形式 gratum，得到「合某人的心意、讨某人喜欢」这一意思。

items.en: Old French agreer, from the phrase a gré 'to someone's liking', meant 'to please, to be agreeable'; the noun agrement named pleasure or consent.
items.cn: 古法语 agreer 出自短语 a gré「合乎某人的心意」，意为「使满意、合意」；同族名词 agrement 表示愉快或同意。

items.en: Middle English agreen first meant 'to please or be pleasing'; the sense 'to be of one mind' is recorded later, and exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 agreen 最初意为「使满意、令人愉快」；「意见相同」的义项出现较晚，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word then spread along five lines: consent, joint decisions, matching accounts, grammatical concord and the suitability of food.
items.cn: 此后这个词沿五条线展开：答应、共同决定、账目相符、语法一致，以及食物是否合胃口。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same pleasing root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of consenting and matching, which differ in formality and in what they accept.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「合意」词根构成的词；近义组收表示同意与相符的动词，彼此在正式程度和接受对象上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for a contract, for consent, or for the state of matching.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协议、同意、一致」，由本词加后缀 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Pleasant or acceptable; it keeps the old sense of being to someone's liking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的、可接受的」，保留了「合人心意」这一古老含义。

entries.definition: To have a different opinion, or of figures, not to match.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同意、不一致」，由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: A difference of opinion or a failure to match.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分歧、不一致」，由 disagree 加后缀 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: To give permission for something; narrower than agree and usually formal or legal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「准许、同意」，比 agree 范围窄，多用于正式或法律语境。

entries.definition: To share an opinion, especially in a formal or written judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意、意见相同」，多用于正式表态或书面判断，语气比 agree 郑重。

entries.definition: To accept a proposal or suggestion, usually after considering it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赞同、应允」，通常指考虑之后接受某项提议，属正式用词。

entries.definition: To match or be equivalent, used of things rather than opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「相符、对应」，用于事物之间的吻合，而不是人的看法。

entries.definition: To be consistent with something, or to grant something formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「与……相符」或「正式给予」，前一种用法与 agree 的「相符」义接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts ad- and gratum, the recorded family, and the prepositions that change the meaning.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语部件 ad- 与 gratum、有记录的词族，以及会改变词义的几个介词。

normal.en: Ad- is 'to' and gratum is 'pleasing': to agree is to be pleasing to someone, that is, to fall in with their view.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，gratum 是「合意的」：agree 本义是合某人的心意，也就是与他的看法合到一处。

normal.en: Three prepositions mark three relations: agree with a person, agree to a proposal, agree on a point.
normal.cn: 三个介词标出三种关系：agree with 对人，agree to 对提议，agree on 对具体一点。

normal.en: Agreement is the state or the document; agreeable is the pleasant quality of the same stem.
normal.cn: agreement 是状态或文件，agreeable 是同一词干表示「令人愉快」的形容词。

normal.en: In grammar the verb agrees with its subject: the two endings must fall into line.
normal.cn: 语法上说动词与主语 agree，意思是两边的词尾必须对齐。

normal.en: Food that does not agree with you is food your body refuses to fall in with.
normal.cn: 食物与你不 agree，就是身体不肯接受它。

abstract.en: Picture two lines bending until they touch at a single point.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线各自弯过来，最后在一个点上相接。

abstract.en: The same point of contact can be an opinion, a price, two columns of figures, or a verb ending.
abstract.cn: 同一个接点可以是一种看法、一个价格、两列数字，或一个动词词尾。

abstract.en: Agreeing is not becoming the same: the two lines keep their direction and touch only where they chose.
abstract.cn: 同意不是变成一样：两条线各自保有方向，只在它们选定的地方相接。

examples.en: I agree with you that the plan needs more time.
examples.cn: 我同意你的看法，这个计划还需要更多时间。

examples.en: The two sides agreed on a price after a long night of talks.
examples.cn: 经过一整夜的谈判，双方就价格达成了一致。

examples.en: In this sentence the verb must agree with its subject in number.
examples.cn: 在这个句子里，动词必须在数上与主语保持一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额格瑞」——额头上一点，两个人格的看法在那个点上重合：同意、一致。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」加 gratum「合意的、令人愉快的」（gratus 的中性形式），经古法语 agreer「使满意、合意」进入英语；核心是「合到某人的心意上」，再引申为人与人、物与物的「对得上」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of agree all describe one point where two things meet: two opinions, a request and a yes, two negotiating sides, two sets of figures, subject and verb, or food and a body.
sensesIntro.cn: agree 的六个义项都在描述同一个「相接之点」：两种看法、一个请求与一声应允、谈判双方、两组数字、主语与谓语，或食物与身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines coming from different directions bend and touch at one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条来自不同方向的线弯过来，在一个点上相接。

branches.en: OPINION: two minds meet at one view, and the word needs with.
branches.cn: 看法线：两个心意在一个看法上相接，这一用法常带 with。

branches.en: CONSENT: the meeting is between a request and a nod.
branches.cn: 应允线：接点落在请求与点头之间。

branches.en: BARGAIN: two sides land on the same arrangement, which is why on follows the verb.
branches.cn: 商定线：双方落到同一个安排上，所以动词后面常跟 on 点出落点。

branches.en: MATCHING: things and grammar join the same pattern, with figures or with endings.
branches.cn: 吻合线：事物与语法也套进同一模式，比的是数字或词尾。

branches.en: THE BODY: food meets a constitution, and the oldest sense of pleasing returns.
branches.cn: 身体线：食物与体质相接，最古老的「合意」义在这里回来了。

intro.en: Agree comes from a Latin prefix plus a Latin adjective, filtered through Old French; English then adds -ment, -able and dis- to build the family.
intro.cn: agree 由拉丁语前缀加一个拉丁语形容词构成，经古法语过滤后进入英语，英语再用 -ment、-able 与 dis- 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Gratus, gratia and the derived forms are all recorded Latin words; the French verb agreer is likewise attested, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: gratus、gratia 及其派生形式都是有记录的拉丁语词，法语动词 agreer 同样有文献可查，因此这里没有重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它把词义朝向那个被取悦的人。

items.example: It is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族背后的那个形容词。

items.example: Ad plus this form gives the sense of falling in with someone.
items.exampleCN: ad 加上这个形式，就有了「合某人心意」的意思。

items.example: It shows the same root in a noun shape.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了同一词根的名词形态。

items.example: Old French carried the word towards English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个词带向英语。

items.example: It forms agreement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agreement。

items.example: It forms agreeable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agreeable。

items.example: It forms disagree.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disagree。

items.example: It forms agreeably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agreeably。

definition_zh: 协议；协定；同意；意见一致；相符；（语法）一致关系
definition_en: a formal arrangement reached between people, the act or state of agreeing, or the matching of forms in grammar
core_image: 双方在同一页纸的末尾各签一个名字，两条线在同一处接上
scene: 谈判室的门终于开了，双方把文件摊在长桌上，一页页翻看并签字。The two sides reached an agreement after three days of talks.
sceneCN: 这里 agreement 是「协议、协定」（第 1 个义项：正式谈成的书面安排）；句意为双方经过三天会谈达成了一项协议。长桌、文件与签字构成画面。

pos.zh: 名词：协议、协定；同意；一致、相符；（语法）一致关系

collocations.zh: 关于……的协议或一致意见

由同一词干加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人愉快的；可接受的」

由 disagree 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「分歧；不一致」

senses.title: A formal arrangement
senses.definition: a formal arrangement or contract made between people, groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团体或国家之间达成的正式安排或合约
senses.example: The company signed an agreement to supply parts for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司签署了一份为期五年的零件供应协议。
senses.why: Once shared consent is written into clauses and signed, the state of agreeing becomes an object you can hold, so the noun names the document itself.
senses.whyCN: 把彼此合意写成条款并签上名字之后，那份「意见相合」就变成了一件可以拿在手里的东西，于是名词直接指文件本身。

senses.title: The act of consenting
senses.definition: the act of saying yes to a request or of accepting a proposal
senses.definitionCN: 对请求表示应允或对提议表示接受的行为
senses.example: Her agreement to help came as a relief to the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她答应帮忙，让整个团队松了一口气。
senses.why: The -ment ending turns the verb's nod into a thing: agree is the nodding, agreement is the nod itself, viewed as an event.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词的「点头」变成一个名词：agree 是点头的动作，agreement 是把这次点头当作一件事来看。

senses.title: Shared opinion
senses.definition: the state of having the same opinion, or the fact that people think alike
senses.definitionCN: 人们持有相同看法，或想法趋于一致的状态
senses.example: There is broad agreement among scientists on this point.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个问题上，科学家们有广泛的共识。
senses.why: Here the meeting point is inside a group: many separate minds overlap, and the overlap, not any document, is what the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这里的接点落在一群人内部：许多各自的想法重叠在一起，这个词指的就是那片重叠，而不是任何文件。

senses.title: Correspondence between things
senses.definition: the state of two accounts, sets of figures or descriptions matching each other
senses.definitionCN: 两份记录、两组数字或两种描述彼此吻合的状态
senses.example: The agreement between the two reports was too exact to be a coincidence.
senses.exampleCN: 两份报告吻合得如此精确，不可能是巧合。
senses.why: Shift the meeting point from people to records: two accounts that fit together line by line are said to be in agreement, just as two minds were.
senses.whyCN: 把接点从人移到记录上：两份说法逐条对得上，也像两个人谈拢一样被称作 agreement，这时它说的是物与物的吻合。

senses.title: Grammatical concord
senses.definition: the matching of number, person or gender between words that are grammatically connected
senses.definitionCN: 有语法关系的词之间在数、人称或性上相互匹配
senses.example: The teacher marked every failure of agreement between subject and verb.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把每一处主谓不一致都标了出来。
senses.why: Grammar takes the everyday idea of fitting and makes it a rule: two endings that do not meet are recorded as an error called agreement.
senses.whyCN: 语法把日常的「对得上」做成规则：两个词尾接不上，就被记成一处叫作 agreement 的错误，于是这个名词也成了语法术语。

intro.en: Agreement is the noun built on agree, with the French suffix -ment; its root is Latin gratus 'pleasing'.
intro.cn: agreement 是在 agree 之上加法语名词后缀 -ment 构成的名词，词根是拉丁语 gratus「令人愉快的」。

items.en: Gratus meant 'pleasing, welcome, thankful', and gratia 'grace, favour' came from the same stem.
items.cn: gratus 意为「令人愉快的、受欢迎的、感激的」，gratia「恩惠、好意」也出自同一词干。

items.en: Ad 'to' plus gratum 'pleasing' gave the sense 'to be in someone's favour', the seed of both agree and agreement.
items.cn: ad「朝向」加 gratum「合意的」，得到「合某人心意」的意思，这是 agree 与 agreement 共同的种子。

items.en: The verb agreer 'to please' and its noun agrement 'pleasure, consent' supplied both the verb and the ending used in English.
items.cn: 动词 agreer「使满意」与它的名词 agrement「愉快、同意」，同时提供了英语所用的动词与名词词尾。

items.en: Middle English agreement first named the state of being pleased or of sharing a view; the legal sense 'a contract' is recorded later, and exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 中古英语 agreement 最初指「感到满意」或「看法相同」的状态；法律上「合约」的义项出现较晚，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law, diplomacy, business and grammar each took the word over: a written contract, a shared opinion, and a rule that matching endings must meet.
items.cn: 法律、外交、商业与语法各自接管了这个词：一份书面合约、一种共同看法，以及词尾必须对齐的一条规则。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb and adjectives of the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers other names for contracts, permission and shared opinion.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干的动词与形容词；近义组收表示合约、许可与共识的其他名词。

entries.definition: The verb that agreement is built on: to share an opinion, consent, or match.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意、一致、适合」，是 agreement 所依附的基础词。

entries.definition: Pleasant or willing; it keeps the oldest sense of being to someone's liking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人愉快的、乐意的」，保留了「合人心意」这一最古老的含义。

entries.definition: To hold a different opinion, or of figures, not to match.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同意、不一致」，由否定前缀 dis- 加 agree 构成。

entries.definition: A difference of opinion, or a failure of two things to match.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分歧、不一致」，与 agreement 结构相同而意义相反。

entries.definition: A written arrangement that the law can enforce; narrower and more formal than agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「合同」，指可依法执行的书面安排，比 agreement 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: A formal written agreement between states.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条约」，专指国家之间正式的书面协议。

entries.definition: A general agreement among a group, with no document involved.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共识」，指一群人的普遍一致，不涉及文件。

entries.definition: Permission given by one side, not a mutual arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「许可、同意」，是单方面给出的允许，而非双方共同的安排。

entries.definition: A formal agreement, often between nations; also the state of being in harmony.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协定、一致」，多用于国家之间，也可指和谐的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real suffix -ment, the family forms, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的后缀 -ment、这一词族的形式，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns the verb agree into a thing: a state, or a document.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ment 把动词 agree 变成一样东西：一种状态，或一份文件。

normal.en: A signed agreement is consent written down and dated.
normal.cn: 签了字的 agreement，就是把「同意」写下来并注明日期。

normal.en: In agreement with marks matching, not necessarily permission.
normal.cn: in agreement with 标出的是「对得上」，不一定是「准许」。

normal.en: Grammarians speak of agreement when subject and verb share number.
normal.cn: 语法学家说 agreement，是指主语和动词在数上一致。

normal.en: One word covers both a sheet of paper and a room full of nodding heads.
normal.cn: 同一个词既指一页纸，也指一屋子点头的人。

abstract.en: Picture two signatures meeting at the foot of the same page.
abstract.cn: 想象两个签名在同一页纸的末尾碰在一起。

abstract.en: The same meeting can be a contract, a nodding room, or two columns of matching figures.
abstract.cn: 同一个「相接」可以是一份合约、一屋子点头的人，或两列对得上的数字。

abstract.en: An agreement does not erase the two parties; it joins them at one point only.
abstract.cn: 协议不会抹掉双方，它只在一个点上把双方接起来。

examples.en: The company signed an agreement to supply parts for five years.
examples.cn: 这家公司签署了一份为期五年的零件供应协议。

examples.en: There is broad agreement among scientists on this point.
examples.cn: 在这个问题上，科学家们有广泛的共识。

examples.en: The teacher marked every failure of agreement between subject and verb.
examples.cn: 老师把每一处主谓不一致都标了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额格瑞门特」——两扇门在同一处合上，门后摆着一份签好的文件：协议、一致。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「朝向」加 gratum「合意的」构成「合意」这一概念，经古法语 agreer 与名词 agrement 进入英语，再加上名词后缀 -ment 定型；核心仍是「两条线在同一处接上」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of agreement all name one meeting point, seen either as a signed document, a nod, a shared view, a matching pair of records, or a pair of matching word endings.
sensesIntro.cn: agreement 的五个义项都指同一个接点，只是看它的角度不同：签好的文件、一声应允、一片共同看法、两份对得上的记录，或两个对齐的词尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures meet at the foot of one page, joining two parties at a single point.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个签名在同一页纸的末尾相接，把双方在一个点上连起来。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: consent written into clauses becomes a thing with a date and signatures.
branches.cn: 文件线：写进条款的同意，变成有日期、有签名的实物。

branches.en: THE NOD: the same consent viewed as a single act rather than a paper.
branches.cn: 点头线：同一份同意被当作一次行为，而不是一张纸。

branches.en: THE GROUP: many minds overlap, and the overlap itself is the agreement.
branches.cn: 人群线：许多想法重叠，重叠的那片区域本身就是 agreement。

branches.en: THE RECORDS: two accounts fit line by line, with no people involved.
branches.cn: 记录线：两份说法逐条对得上，此时不涉及人。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: the matching becomes a rule, and a failure to match becomes an error.
branches.cn: 语法线：这种相合被定为规则，对不上就成了错误。

definition_zh: 农业；农艺；农学；耕作；农业部门
definition_en: the practice and science of farming, including growing crops and raising animals, or the farming sector of an economy
core_image: 犁尖翻开一道田垄，一行行作物从土里长出来
scene: 山坡上一层层水田泛着亮光，清晨有人牵着水牛下田。Agriculture still employs most of the people in this valley.
sceneCN: 这里 agriculture 是「农业」（第 1 个义项：种植与饲养构成的生产整体）；句意为农业仍然是这个山谷里大多数人的生计。水田、水牛与晨雾构成画面。

forms.label: 不可数名词（通常无复数）

senses.title: Farming as a whole
senses.definition: the practice of growing crops and raising animals for food, fibre or other products
senses.definitionCN: 种植作物、饲养牲畜以获取食物、纤维或其他产品的生产活动
senses.example: Agriculture shaped the landscape of this plain for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 农业塑造了这片平原的地貌，已持续数千年。
senses.why: Latin ager 'field' plus cultura 'cultivation' says the whole thing at once: the field and the work done on it, taken as one enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ager「田地」加 cultura「耕作」，一句话就说全了：那块田加上对它做的事，合起来当作一项生产事业，就是「农业」。

senses.title: The science and technique of farming
senses.definition: the systematic knowledge and technique of cultivating soil, crops and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 关于耕作土壤、栽培作物与饲养牲畜的系统知识与技术
senses.example: She studied agriculture for four years before returning to the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她学了四年农学，然后回到家里的农场。
senses.why: Cultura already meant both tilling and training; once the tilling is set out as teachable knowledge, the word becomes a discipline.
senses.whyCN: cultura 本来就兼指「耕作」与「培养、训练」；当耕作被整理成可以教、可以学的知识时，这个词就成了一门学科。

senses.title: Tilling the soil
senses.definition: the physical work of preparing and cultivating land, the oldest and most literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 翻整与照料土地的具体劳作，是最古老、最字面的义项
senses.example: In the old handbook, agriculture meant ploughing, sowing and harvest in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧手册里，「agriculture」依次指耕地、播种与收获。
senses.why: This is the etymological core laid bare: ager is the plot, cultura is the turning and tending, and together they name work done with hands.
senses.whyCN: 这是词源最直白的一面：ager 是那块地，cultura 是翻土与照料，合起来就是「用手在一块地上干活」。

senses.title: The farming sector
senses.definition: farming as a branch of the economy or a field of government policy
senses.definitionCN: 作为国民经济的一个门类或政府政策领域来看的农业
senses.example: Subsidies to agriculture account for a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 对农业的补贴占了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: When tilling is counted, taxed and subsidised, the field becomes a line in a table, and the word shifts from the work to the sector.
senses.whyCN: 当耕作要被统计、征税和补贴时，田地就变成了表格里的一栏，这个词也就从田间劳作转指整个产业部门。

senses.title: Farming as a livelihood
senses.definition: farming considered as the means by which a place or a people lives
senses.definitionCN: 作为某地或某群人赖以为生的手段来看的农业
senses.example: For most families here, agriculture is the only source of income.
senses.exampleCN: 对这里的大多数家庭来说，农业是唯一的收入来源。
senses.why: The field feeds the people who work it, so the same word can name not a technique or a sector but the living that land provides.
senses.whyCN: 田地不只长出粮食，也养活靠它的人；因此这个词还可以不指技术、不指部门，而指土地提供的那份生计。

intro.en: Agriculture is a Latin compound of ager 'field' and cultura 'cultivation', and it entered English as a bookish word for the tilling of land.
intro.cn: agriculture 是拉丁语 ager「田地」与 cultura「耕作」的复合词，进入英语时是一个书面色彩较浓的「耕地」之词。

items.en: *h₂éǵros is the reconstructed root for 'field'; it is the common ancestor of Latin ager, Greek agros and English acre, and the reconstruction is marked as such.
items.cn: 重构形式 *h₂éǵros 表示「田地」，是拉丁语 ager、希腊语 agros 与英语 acre 的共同祖先；此处标明它是重构形式。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, land, countryside'; its genitive agri shows the stem agr- that appears in compounds.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、土地、乡野」；其属格 agri 显示出复合词中出现的词干 agr-。

items.en: Colere meant 'to till, cultivate, inhabit, worship'; the noun cultura named cultivation and, by extension, care and training.
items.cn: colere 意为「耕作、栽培、居住、敬奉」；名词 cultura 表示耕作，并引申出照料与培养。

items.en: Ager plus cultura formed agricultura, 'the cultivation of land', a word already used by Roman writers on farming.
items.cn: ager 加 cultura 构成 agricultura「土地耕作」，罗马的农书作者已经使用这个词。

items.en: English agriculture is recorded from the fifteenth century, probably through French; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 agriculture 自十五世纪起有记录，可能经法语传入；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widened from work in the field to a science, an industry, a ministry and a subject at university.
items.cn: 这个词从田间的劳作扩展为一门科学、一个产业、一个政府部门，以及大学里的一门专业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the ager- root, either through Latin or through Greek and Old English; the near-meaning group gathers narrower words for working the land.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 ager- 词根上的词，或经拉丁语，或经希腊语与古英语；近义组收范围更窄的「种地」类词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of or relating to farming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「农业的、农艺的」，由本词加后缀 -al 构成。

entries.definition: A person who practises or studies farming.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农学家、务农者」，由本词加后缀 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: The science of crop production; Greek agros 'field' matches Latin ager, so the root is shared but the path differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农学、作物学」；希腊语 agros「田地」与拉丁语 ager 同出印欧语田地词根，词根相同而传入路径不同。

entries.definition: A unit of land area; Old English æcer came from the same Indo-European word for a field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「英亩」；古英语 æcer 与 ager 同出印欧语表示「田地」的词。

entries.definition: Farming treated as a large commercial industry; a modern compound with agriculture as its first half.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农业综合企业」，指把农业当作大型商业产业来经营，是 agriculture 与 business 构成的现代复合词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for growing crops and keeping animals, including the business side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「务农、耕作」，是最日常的说法，也包含经营的一面。

entries.definition: The careful management of soil, crops or animals; old-fashioned and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农牧管理、耕作」，强调精心经营，语气正式且偏旧。

entries.definition: The act of preparing land and growing crops; narrower than agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耕作、栽培」，只指整地与种植这一动作，范围比 agriculture 窄。

entries.definition: The growing of garden plants, fruit and vegetables, on a smaller scale than agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「园艺」，指园圃里种植花木果蔬，规模比农业小。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin halves ager and cultura, the recorded family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语两半 ager 与 cultura、有记录的词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ager is 'field' and cultura is 'cultivation': agriculture is literally field-cultivation.
normal.cn: ager 是「田地」，cultura 是「耕作」：agriculture 字面就是「耕田」。

normal.en: The same field root appears in acre and, through Greek, in agronomy.
normal.cn: 同一个「田地」词根还出现在 acre 里，并经由希腊语出现在 agronomy 里。

normal.en: Cultura also gives culture: both words are about tending something and bringing it on.
normal.cn: cultura 还给出 culture：两个词都与「照料并让它成长」有关。

normal.en: Agricultural and agriculturist are the two common family forms.
normal.cn: agricultural 与 agriculturist 是这一词族最常用的两个形式。

normal.en: The Ministry of Agriculture is the sector sense: farming counted as a branch of government.
normal.cn: the Ministry of Agriculture 用的是部门义：农业被算作政府的一个分支。

abstract.en: Picture a plough turning one dark strip of soil, with a row of green shoots behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象犁头翻起一条深色的土，后面已有一行绿苗。

abstract.en: The same field is a workplace, a science, a budget line and a way of life.
abstract.cn: 同一块田可以是干活的地方、一门科学、一行预算，和一种活法。

abstract.en: The word joins two halves: the land that is given, and the care that is added to it.
abstract.cn: 这个词把两半合在一起：被给予的土地，和加上去的照料。

examples.en: Agriculture shaped the landscape of this plain for thousands of years.
examples.cn: 农业塑造了这片平原的地貌，已持续数千年。

examples.en: She studied agriculture for four years before returning to the family farm.
examples.cn: 她学了四年农学，然后回到家里的农场。

examples.en: Subsidies to agriculture account for a large share of the budget.
examples.cn: 对农业的补贴占了预算的很大一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安格瑞扣」——阿格在田里一扣一翻，土开了花：农业、耕作。

root: 拉丁语 ager「田地、土地」加 cultura「耕作、栽培」（源自 colere「耕作、照料」）构成 agricultura；原始印欧语 *h₂éǵros「田地」为重构形式，是 ager、希腊语 agros 与英语 acre 的共同来源。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of agriculture keep the same pair of halves, land and care: as a whole enterprise, a science, hand work in the soil, an economic sector, or a livelihood.
sensesIntro.cn: agriculture 的五个义项都保留同样两半，即土地与照料：作为整体生产、作为科学、作为土里的手工、作为经济部门，或作为生计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plough turns a strip of dark soil, and green shoots follow behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：犁头翻开一条深色泥土，后面跟着一行绿苗。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: field plus work becomes one enterprise of growing and raising.
branches.cn: 生产线：田地加劳作合成为一项种植与饲养的事业。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the same work, written down as teachable knowledge, becomes agronomy.
branches.cn: 科学线：同样的劳作被写成可教的知识，就成了农学。

branches.en: SOIL: the oldest layer, where hands actually turn the earth.
branches.cn: 土壤线：最古老的一层，手真的在翻土。

branches.en: SECTOR: counted and subsidised, the field becomes a column in a budget.
branches.cn: 部门线：一旦被统计和补贴，田地就成了预算表上的一栏。

branches.en: LIVELIHOOD: the land also feeds the people who work it.
branches.cn: 生计线：土地同时也养活靠它劳作的人。

intro.en: Agriculture is a Latin noun compounded of a field word and a cultivation word; English adds only ordinary endings on top.
intro.cn: agriculture 是由「田地」与「耕作」两个拉丁语词合成的名词，英语只在上面添加普通词尾。

latinIntro.en: Ager, colere, cultura and agricultura are recorded Latin words; only the Indo-European root for 'field' is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: ager、colere、cultura 与 agricultura 都是有记录的拉丁语词，只有表示「田地」的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个复合词的前一半。

items.example: It is the shape the root takes inside compounds.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词根在复合词内部取的形式。

items.example: It is the verb behind cultura.
items.exampleCN: 它是 cultura 背后的动词。

items.example: It supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了这个复合词的后一半。

items.example: It joins the field root with a word for a tiller.
items.exampleCN: 它把田地词根与表示耕作者的部分合在一起。

items.example: It is the compound that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 它就是英语借用的那个复合词。

items.example: It forms agricultural.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agricultural。

items.example: It forms agriculturist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agriculturist。

items.example: It forms agriculturally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agriculturally。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「农业的；农艺的」
由 agricultural 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在农业方面」
由本词加名词后缀 -ist 构成，义为「农学家；务农者」
由 agricultural 加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「农学家；农业经营者」

definition_zh: 在前面；向前；提前；领先；将来；（ahead of）超前于、优于
definition_en: further forward in space or time than someone or something else, or in a better position in a race or a process
core_image: 船头朝前：身体最前端的头先探进还没看清的水面
scene: 雾还没散的江面上，渔船排成一列缓缓下行，船头压出白色水纹。The lead boat moved ahead of the others and vanished into the mist.
sceneCN: 这里 ahead 是「在前面」（第 1 个义项：空间位置更靠前）；句意为领头的船驶到其他船前面，消失在雾里。画面里是江面、船队与船头的水纹。

pos.zh: 副词：在前面；向前；提前；领先；将来
形容词（多作表语）：领先的；走在前面的

derivatives.zh: 由短语 go ahead 凝固而成，义为「许可、放行」或「有进取心的」
由短语 look ahead 合成，义为「前瞻、预先判断」，多用于技术与决策语境
由 straight ahead 合成，义为「直截了当的、不加花饰的」，也形容音乐风格纯正

senses.title: Further forward in space
senses.definition: in or into a position further forward than someone or something else
senses.definitionCN: 处于或进入比某人、某物更靠前的位置
senses.example: She walked ahead and held the gate open for us.
senses.exampleCN: 她走在前面，替我们把大门撑着。
senses.why: The second part of the word is head, the front of a body; whoever is ahead has that front point further along than the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的后半是 head「头」，也就是身体最前端；谁的头更靠前，谁就在前面，所以 ahead 直接指位置上的靠前。

senses.title: Earlier than planned
senses.definition: before the time that was planned, expected or agreed
senses.definitionCN: 在计划、预期或约定的时间之前
senses.example: The bridge was finished three months ahead of the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥比截止期限提前三个月完工。
senses.why: Space in front is mapped onto the time line: an event that stands in front of its scheduled point has reached it early.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「靠前」被投射到时间轴上：一件事跑到了预定时刻的前面，就是提前完成，这也是英语常用「前」表示「早」的原因。

senses.title: Leading in a race or contest
senses.titleCN: 领先：在比赛或进程中占先
senses.definition: in front of rivals in a race, competition or ranking
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞争或排名中位于对手之前
senses.example: By the second lap she was already ahead by ten metres.
senses.exampleCN: 到第二圈时她已经领先十米。
senses.why: A race is decided by whose head crosses the line first, so the plain spatial sense is read straight off as leading.
senses.whyCN: 比赛看的就是谁的头先越过终点线，所以「位置靠前」不需要另造词，直接就读作「领先」。

senses.title: Into the future
senses.definition: in or toward the future, especially when thinking about what will come
senses.definitionCN: 在未来或朝向未来，尤指考虑将要发生的事时
senses.example: The report looks ahead to the next decade of energy use.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告展望了未来十年的能源使用。
senses.why: People walk facing forward, so the direction the head points is where time has not yet arrived; that direction is the future.
senses.whyCN: 人走路时面朝前方，头所朝的方向正是时间尚未抵达之处；顺着这个朝向看过去，「前方」就成了「将来」。

senses.title: Onward with an action
senses.titleCN: 继续向前：把动作推进下去
senses.definition: continuing forward with an action or plan rather than stopping
senses.definitionCN: 不停下来，把某个行动或计划继续推行下去
senses.example: The council decided to go ahead with the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 议会决定继续推进新图书馆的工程。
senses.why: If the head keeps pointing forward and the body keeps moving, the word naturally means not stopping; go ahead is that image turned into a phrase.
senses.whyCN: 头一直朝前、身体一直移动，这个词自然就有了「不停下」的意思；go ahead 正是把这个画面凝固成了短语。

senses.title: More advanced than its time
senses.definition: more advanced than the period or the people around it, as in ahead of its time
senses.definitionCN: 比所处时代或周围人更先进，如短语 ahead of its time
senses.example: Her design was years ahead of its time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的设计超前于它所属的时代好些年。
senses.why: Something standing further forward than its own generation looks as if it has already arrived in the future, so being ahead becomes being advanced.
senses.whyCN: 一个东西比同代人站得更靠前，看上去就像已经抵达了未来，于是「在前的」引申为「超前的、先进的」。

intro.en: Ahead is not a Latin borrowing but a native English compound: a weakened preposition plus the old word for the head of a body.
intro.cn: ahead 不是拉丁语借词，而是英语本土的复合词：一个弱化的介词加上表示「头」的古词。

items.en: Hēafod meant the head of a person or animal, and by extension the top or front end of anything.
items.cn: hēafod 指人或动物的头，引申也指任何东西的顶端或前端。

items.en: The form is generally explained as a- (a weakened form of on, 'on, at') plus head, giving the sense 'at the head, in front'.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词形由 a-（on「在……上」的弱化形式）加 head 构成，意思是「在头部的位置、在前方」。

items.en: The adverb is recorded in the seventeenth century, first in nautical language for a ship further forward than another.
items.cn: 这个副词在十七世纪有记录，最早出现在航海用语里，指一条船比另一条更靠前。

items.en: The sense widens from ships to any forward position, and then to time, giving ahead of schedule and ahead of time.
items.cn: 词义从船只扩展到任何靠前的位置，再扩展到时间，于是有了 ahead of schedule 与 ahead of time。

items.en: Whether the a- came from on or from at is source uncertain; the compound itself and its 'front' meaning are not in doubt.
items.cn: 这个 a- 究竟来自 on 还是 at，来源不确定；但复合词本身及其「在前」的含义并无争议。

note.en: The first group gathers words built with the same head element; the second gathers words that also point forward in space or time.
note.cn: 第一组收的是同样以 head 为核心成分构成的词；第二组收的也是指向空间或时间前方的词。

entries.definition: The body part, or the top or front of anything; it is the second element inside ahead, not a synonym of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「头、顶端、前端」；它是 ahead 内部的第二个成分，本身并不是 ahead 的同义词。

entries.definition: Progress made against difficulty, as in make headway; built from head plus way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进展」，常见于 make headway；由 head 加 way 构成，与 ahead 共用 head。

entries.definition: Above the level of the head; a different compound, built with over rather than with a-.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」；是另一个复合词，用 over 而非 a- 构成，只是同样含 head。

entries.definition: With the head first, or with reckless speed; the old suffix -long marks direction.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「头朝前地、鲁莽地」；古后缀 -long 表示方向，同样以 head 为核心。

entries.definition: Toward the front; the general direction word, with no reference point implied.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「向前」，是一般性的方向词，不预设参照物。

entries.definition: Earlier than an event, usually by preparation; covers only the time sense of ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「预先、事先」，多指事前准备；只对应 ahead 的时间义。

entries.definition: Before the expected time, often as an arrangement; a phrase rather than a single adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「提前、预先」，常指事先安排；是短语而非单词副词。

entries.definition: In first place in a contest; stresses rank rather than position.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「领先的、居首的」，强调名次而非空间位置。

entries.definition: Continuing forward in travel or in a process; literary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「继续向前」，用于行程或过程，语气偏书面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the real pieces of the compound and with the phrases the word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用的是这个复合词真实的组成部分，以及它实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Take the two pieces apart: a- plus head, so the head is the part that is out in front.
normal.cn: 把两部分拆开看：a- 加 head，头正是伸在最前面的那部分。

normal.en: A ship that is ahead has its bow nearer the horizon than the ships behind it.
normal.cn: 一条 ahead 的船，船头比后面的船更靠近地平线。

normal.en: Go ahead keeps the picture of motion: the head keeps pointing, the body keeps moving.
normal.cn: go ahead 保留了那个移动的画面：头一直朝前，身体就一直走。

normal.en: Ahead of schedule borrows the same front position and places it on a calendar.
normal.cn: ahead of schedule 借用同一个「靠前位置」，把它放到日历上。

normal.en: Look ahead turns the body's forward direction into a look at the future.
normal.cn: look ahead 把身体朝前的方向变成对未来的张望。

abstract.en: Picture a line of walkers in fog: you can see only the back of the person just ahead of you.
abstract.cn: 想象浓雾里一列行走的人：你只看得见正前方那个人的后背。

abstract.en: Now slide that line onto a clock: the walker in front is the event that arrives early.
abstract.cn: 再把这一列人滑到钟面上：走在最前面的，就是提前抵达的那件事。

abstract.en: In a race the whole word shrinks to a chest and a line: the first chest ahead wins.
abstract.cn: 到了赛场上，整个词缩成一副胸膛和一条终点线：先到线前的那副胸膛赢。

examples.en: The guide went ahead to check that the path was safe.
examples.cn: 向导先走到前面，去查看那条小路是否安全。

examples.en: We finished the report two days ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 我们比预定时间提前两天完成了报告。

examples.en: Looking ahead, the company expects steady growth in Asia.
examples.cn: 展望未来，公司预计在亚洲会稳步增长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呃，黑德」——头一低就往前冲，冲在别人前面

root: 古英语 hēafod「头」加弱化前缀 a-（一般认为来自 on「在……上」），合起来是「在头的位置、朝头的方向」，即「在前面」；十七世纪先在航海语中指船位靠前，后扩展到时间与竞争。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all start from one point in space: the head, the front of a body, which is why ahead can mean in front, earlier, leading, in the future, onward, or advanced for its time.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都从空间上的一个点出发：头，也就是身体的最前端；正因为参照的是「头的位置」，ahead 才能表示在前面、提前、领先、将来、继续推进，以及超前于时代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the front of a body, the head, is the point that measures how far forward something is.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体最前端的头，就是衡量一样东西靠前多少的基准点。

branches.en: SPACE: one object's front point lies beyond another's, so it is simply in front.
branches.cn: 空间线：一个物体的前端超出另一个物体，就是单纯地「在前面」。

branches.en: TIME: the same front point is placed on a schedule, and standing in front of the date means arriving early.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一个前端点被放到日程上，站到日期前面就是提前抵达。

branches.en: CONTEST: in a race the front point is the chest that crosses the line first, which reads as leading.
branches.cn: 竞争线：赛场上这个前端点就是先过线的胸膛，于是读作领先。

branches.en: FUTURE: the direction the head faces is the part of the time line not yet reached.
branches.cn: 未来线：头所朝的方向，就是时间轴上尚未抵达的那一段。

branches.en: PROCESS: keeping the head forward becomes going on with an action, and standing too far forward becomes being ahead of one's time.
branches.cn: 进程线：头一直朝前就是继续推进，而站得过于靠前则成了超前于时代。

intro.en: Ahead is a native compound, so its parts are English elements rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: ahead 是英语本土复合词，因此它的构件是英语成分，而不是拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here, so no Latin cognates are listed; the deeper Germanic material is reconstructed only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，因此不列拉丁同源词；更早的日耳曼语材料只属重构形式。

items.example: It also appears in ashore and asleep.
items.exampleCN: 这个弱化前缀也出现在 ashore 与 asleep 里。

items.meaning: the top or front part of a body
items.example: The noun is the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的核心。

items.example: The modern spelling dropped the internal consonant.
items.exampleCN: 现代拼写丢掉了这个词中间的辅音。

items.example: It forms headmaster and headline.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 headmaster 与 headline。

items.meaning: the top or end of something
items.example: It forms spearhead and bridgehead.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 spearhead 与 bridgehead。

items.example: It forms overhead.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 overhead。

items.example: It forms forehead and foredeck.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 forehead 与 foredeck。

items.example: It forms headlong.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 headlong。

items.example: It forms headway and highway.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 headway 与 highway。

definition_zh: 帮助；援助；辅助工具；援助物资；援助款；帮助、援助（动词）；有助于
definition_en: help or support given to a person or a cause, or a device that makes a task easier; as a verb, to help someone or make something easier
core_image: 伸过去的一只手，替对方分担一部分重量
scene: 洪水退去后，仓库门口堆满各地送来的纸箱，志愿者正低头登记清单。Relief workers handed out food aid to families whose homes had been flooded.
sceneCN: 这里 aid 是「援助物资」（第 3 个义项：送往受灾地区的钱物）；句意为救援人员向房屋被淹的家庭发放食品援助。画面里是仓库、纸箱与登记清单的志愿者。

pos.zh: 名词：帮助；援助；辅助器具；援助物资
动词：帮助；援助；有助于

derivatives.zh: 与 aid 同源的借词，由法语加 -e 的形式而来，义为「助手、随员」
由 aid 加 -ed 构成，义为「有辅助的」，多用于 computer-aided 这类复合词
由 un- 加 aided 构成，义为「无外界帮助的、独立完成的」

senses.title: Help given to someone in need
senses.definition: help or support given to a person, group or cause that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要帮助的人、群体或事业的帮助与支持
senses.example: The stranded climbers called for aid as soon as the storm eased.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴一减弱，受困的登山者就呼救求援。
senses.why: Latin adiutare is built from ad- 'to' plus iuvare 'to give strength', so aid is literally strength added to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adiutare 由 ad-「向」加 iuvare「给予力量」构成，所以援助就是把力量加到对方身上，这正是「分担重量」那只手的意思。

senses.title: A device that makes a task easier
senses.definition: an object or piece of equipment that helps a person do something they could not do easily alone
senses.definitionCN: 帮助人完成难以独立完成之事的物件或设备
senses.example: A simple walking aid helped him cross the room after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 术后一副简单的助行器帮他走过了房间。
senses.why: The same added strength is turned into a thing you can hold: a hearing aid or a walking aid supplies the missing force in solid form.
senses.whyCN: 同一份「加上的力量」被做成可以握在手里的东西：助听器、助行架就是把这股缺的力气变成了实体。

senses.title: Money and supplies sent to a region
senses.definition: money, food, medicine or equipment sent to a place or group that urgently needs it
senses.definitionCN: 送往急需帮助的地区或群体的钱、食物、药品或设备
senses.example: Trucks carrying medical aid reached the border before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 运载医疗援助物资的卡车在黎明前抵达边境。
senses.why: Help that can be packed and shipped becomes countable goods, so the abstract noun turns into crates with labels on them.
senses.whyCN: 能被打包运走的帮助成了可清点的货物，于是这个抽象名词变成了贴着标签的一只只箱子。

senses.title: To help a person or group
senses.definition: to help a person or group do something, especially in a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人或某群体做某事，尤指在困难处境中
senses.example: Volunteers aided the rescue teams in searching the rubble.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者协助救援队在废墟中搜寻。
senses.why: The verb puts the noun back into motion: the reaching hand is no longer a thing but an act performed on someone's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词重新变成动作：那只伸出的手不再是一件东西，而是替别人做出来的一下举动。

senses.title: To make a process easier
senses.definition: to make a process or result easier or more likely to happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程或结果更容易发生、更可能实现
senses.example: Regular exercise aids recovery after a long illness.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动有助于久病之后的康复。
senses.why: The one helped is no longer a person but a process; adding strength to digestion or recovery is still the same image, with the body's own work as the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 被帮助的对象从人变成了过程；给消化或康复添一把力，仍是同一个画面，只是接受这股力的是身体自己的运转。

intro.en: Aid reached English from Latin through Old French, and the Latin verb behind it literally means to add strength to someone.
intro.cn: aid 经由古法语来自拉丁语，它背后的拉丁动词字面意思就是「把力量加到某人身上」。

items.en: Iuvare meant 'to help, assist, give pleasure or strength'. It is the simple verb at the base of the family.
items.cn: iuvare 意为「帮助、支援、给予力量或愉悦」，是这一词族最底层的简单动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus iuvare produced adiuvare 'to help'; its frequentative adiutare meant 'to keep helping, lend regular assistance'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 iuvare 构成 adiuvare「帮助」；其反复动词 adiutare 意为「不断帮助、经常援手」。

items.en: The noun adiutorium meant 'help, assistance', and adiutor meant 'a helper'; both show how early the word could name a person and a thing.
items.cn: 名词 adiutorium 意为「帮助、援助」，adiutor 意为「帮手」；两者都说明这个词很早就能指人也指物。

items.en: Old French aide, from the Latin verb, carried the sense of help and assistance into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 aide 源自上述拉丁动词，在诺曼征服之后把「帮助、援助」的意思带入英语。

items.en: English kept aid for help, devices and relief, and borrowed aide again from French for a person who assists; the two spellings now divide the work.
items.cn: 英语把 aid 留给「帮助、器具、救援物资」，又再次从法语借入 aide 专指「助手」；两种拼写如今分工明确。

note.en: The first group is made of words that share the spelling or the Latin help-root; the second group is made of words that also mean giving help or relief.
note.cn: 第一组是同拼写或同「帮助」词根的词；第二组是同样表示给予帮助或救济的词。

entries.definition: A person who helps someone important, such as an assistant to a politician; same sound, but it names a human being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助手、随员」，如政界人士的助理；读音相同，但专指人。

entries.definition: The past form and participle of the verb, or an adjective in compounds such as computer-aided.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词，也可作形容词用于 computer-aided 一类复合词。

entries.definition: Without help from anyone or anything; formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无外界帮助的」，由否定前缀 un- 加 aided 构成。

entries.definition: The name of a disease, formed from the initials of its full medical name; it merely looks similar and comes from another source.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一种免疫缺陷疾病，由其医学全称的首字母构成；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The everyday word for making things easier for someone; broader and less formal than aid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「帮助」，是最日常的说法，范围比 aid 宽，语气也更随意。

entries.definition: To help, usually as a secondary partner rather than the main agent; more formal than help.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「协助」，通常指作为次要一方参与，而非主导者，比 help 正式。

entries.definition: To hold up or back someone over time, financially or emotionally; longer-term than a single act of aid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「支持、支撑」，可指长期的经济或情感支撑，比一次性的 aid 更持久。

entries.definition: Help given to people in disaster or poverty, often as food, money or shelter; the usual word for emergency aid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「救济、救援」，多指灾荒中提供的食物、钱款或住所，是紧急援助的常用词。

entries.definition: Money paid by a government to lower a price or support an industry; a narrow, financial kind of aid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补贴、补助金」，指政府为压低价格或扶持行业而支付的款项，是 aid 中偏财政的一种。

normalIntro.en: The hooks here follow the real Latin verb and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的钩子顺着真实的拉丁动词，以及这个词实际出现的固定搭配。

normal.en: Ad- means to, iuvare means give strength: aid is strength handed over to somebody.
normal.cn: ad- 是「向」，iuvare 是「给力量」：aid 就是把力量递到别人手上。

normal.en: The frequentative adiutare adds the idea of repeated help, not one dramatic rescue.
normal.cn: 反复动词 adiutare 带出「反复帮助」的意思，而不是一次戏剧性的营救。

normal.en: First aid is the help given before any doctor arrives.
normal.cn: first aid 是医生到来之前给的那份帮助。

normal.en: A hearing aid adds strength to a sense that has grown weak.
normal.cn: hearing aid 是给变弱的感官补上力气。

normal.en: Aid is the help itself, while aide is the person who gives it.
normal.cn: aid 是帮助本身，aide 则是提供帮助的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one heavy crate: the second pair of hands takes part of the weight without taking the crate away.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一只很重的箱子：后来那双手分走了一部分重量，却没有把箱子整个接过去。

abstract.en: The same hands can become a walking frame, a box of medicine or a cheque: the shape changes, the added strength does not.
abstract.cn: 同一双手可以变成助行架、一箱药或一张支票：形状变了，补上的那股力气没变。

abstract.en: Aid does not do the whole job for you; it makes the job possible for you to finish.
abstract.cn: 援助并不替你把整件事做完，它只是让你有能力把它做完。

examples.en: The old map was a great aid to us in the dark forest.
examples.cn: 在那片漆黑的森林里，那张旧地图给了我们很大帮助。

examples.en: Several countries sent aid after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，几个国家送来了援助物资。

examples.en: A gentle stretch can aid sleep after a long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后做些轻柔的拉伸有助于睡眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶的」——一只手递过去，对方应了一声「诶」，援助就到了

root: 拉丁语 adiuvare「帮助」由 ad-「向」加 iuvare「给予力量」构成，其反复动词 adiutare 意为「不断帮助」；名词 adiutorium「援助」经古法语 aide 进入英语，成为 aid。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all carry one image, strength added to someone else's load: the help itself, the tool that supplies it, the goods that carry it, the act of giving it, and the process it makes easier.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共用同一个画面——把力量加到别人的负担上：帮助本身、提供这份力量的器具、把帮助装运出去的物资、给出帮助的动作，以及被这份力量推动得更顺的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pair of hands takes part of the weight without taking the whole load.
core.cn: 核心意象：多出来的一双手分走一部分重量，却不把整副担子接走。

branches.en: THE PERSON: help given to someone who cannot carry the load alone.
branches.cn: 人的一线：给予无法独自承担之人的那份帮助。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the added strength is built into a hearing aid or a walking aid.
branches.cn: 器物的一线：补上的力气被做成助听器或助行架。

branches.en: THE CARGO: help that can be packed becomes countable aid on a truck.
branches.cn: 货物的一线：能装箱的帮助成了卡车上一件件可清点的援助物资。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the moment of reaching out, not the thing handed over.
branches.cn: 动作的一线：动词说的是伸手那一刻，而不是递过去的东西。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: when the receiver is digestion or recovery, the same strength becomes a factor that helps things along.
branches.cn: 过程的一线：当接受者是消化或康复时，同一股力气就成了推动事情顺利进行的因素。

intro.en: Aid comes in as a whole French word, but Latin prefixes and English suffixes organise its family.
intro.cn: aid 是作为完整的法语词进入英语的，但拉丁前缀与英语后缀把这个词族组织了起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verbs adiuvare and adiutare, the noun adiutorium and the agent noun adiutor are all attested, so only the deeper Indo-European layer is reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 adiuvare、adiutare，名词 adiutorium 与施事名词 adiutor 均有文献记录，只有更深的印欧语层次属于重构。

items.example: It marks the direction of the help in adiuvare.
items.exampleCN: 在 adiuvare 里，这个前缀标出帮助所朝的方向。

items.example: The verb is the semantic core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的语义核心。

items.example: The repeated action is marked by the suffix -tare.
items.exampleCN: 反复的动作由后缀 -tare 标出。

items.example: It entered English from Old French aide.
items.exampleCN: 它经古法语 aide 进入英语。

items.example: It was borrowed again to name a person.
items.exampleCN: 它被再次借入，用来指人。

items.example: It forms aided.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aided。

items.example: It forms aiding.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aiding。

items.example: It forms unaided.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unaided。

items.example: It forms aid worker and aid agency.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aid worker 与 aid agency。

definition_zh: 目标；目的；瞄准（动作）；瞄准（动词）；旨在；针对
definition_en: a result that a person wants to achieve, or the act of pointing a weapon or camera at something; as a verb, to point at a target or to intend a result
core_image: 弓弦拉满，箭尖压住远处的靶心
scene: 靶场上风很轻，射手把弓举到肩高，眼睛锁住远处的圆心。She raised the rifle and aimed at the centre of the target.
sceneCN: 这里 aim 是「瞄准」（第 3 个义项：把武器或镜头对准某处）；句意为她举起步枪，瞄准靶心。画面里是靶场、弓与远处的圆心。

pos.zh: 名词：目标；目的；瞄准的动作
动词：瞄准；旨在；针对

collocations.zh: 旨在做某事；力争做某事

derivatives.zh: 由 aim 加形容词后缀 -less 构成，义为「无目标的、漫无目的的」
由 aimless 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「漫无目的地」
由 aimless 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「无目标、漫无目的的状态」

senses.title: A purpose or goal
senses.definition: something that a person hopes to achieve by doing something
senses.definitionCN: 一个人希望通过行动达成的结果
senses.example: Her main aim was to finish the race without stopping.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要目标是中途不停跑完全程。
senses.why: To shoot straight you must first fix a point to shoot at; pull that point out of the bow and it becomes the goal of any effort.
senses.whyCN: 要把箭射准，先得定一个可射的点；把这个点从弓上抽出来，它就是任何努力想要抵达的「目标」。

senses.title: The act of taking aim
senses.definition: the act of pointing a weapon or camera at a target, especially in the phrase take aim
senses.definitionCN: 把武器或镜头对准目标的行为，尤见于短语 take aim
senses.example: The archer took aim and released the string.
senses.exampleCN: 弓箭手瞄准后松开了弓弦。
senses.why: This is the noun at its most physical: it names the few seconds between raising the weapon and letting it go.
senses.whyCN: 这是名词最实在的一面：它指的是举起武器到放手之间那几秒钟，动作还没结果，只有对准。

senses.title: To point at a target
senses.definition: to point a weapon, camera or device toward a target
senses.definitionCN: 把武器、镜头或装置朝向某个目标
senses.example: He aimed the telescope at the brightest star in the cluster.
senses.exampleCN: 他把望远镜对准星团中最亮的那颗星。
senses.why: The verb spells out the movement the noun implies: the front end of a thing is turned until it lines up with the target.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词暗含的动作摊开：把某物的前端转过去，直到它与目标连成一条直线。

senses.title: To intend to achieve something
senses.definition: to plan or try to achieve a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 计划或力图取得某个特定结果
senses.example: The new course aims to give students practical lab skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门新课程旨在让学生掌握实用的实验技能。
senses.why: An intention is a target held inside the mind; the action is loosed at it just as an arrow is loosed at a mark.
senses.whyCN: 意图就是立在心里的一枚靶；行动朝它放出去，和箭朝靶心放出去是同一个动作，所以 aim 从「瞄准」转为「旨在」。

senses.title: To direct something at a group
senses.definition: to direct a product, message or action toward a particular group or person
senses.definitionCN: 把产品、讯息或行动对准某一特定群体或个人
senses.example: The campaign is aimed at teenagers who have never voted.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动面向从未投过票的青少年。
senses.why: Replace the paper target with people: whatever is aimed is now pointed at an audience, and the word means targeting rather than shooting.
senses.whyCN: 把纸靶换成人：被对准的东西现在指向一群受众，于是这个词说的是「针对谁」，而不是「射中什么」。

intro.en: Aim comes from Old French, and behind the French verb stands a Latin verb about judging worth, which is why the word once meant estimate before it meant point.
intro.cn: aim 来自古法语，法语动词背后是一个表示「估量价值」的拉丁动词，因此这个词先有「估量」之意，后才有「对准」之意。

items.en: Aestimare meant 'to value, estimate, judge the worth of something', and it also gave English estimate and esteem.
items.cn: aestimare 意为「估价、估量、判断价值」，它也为英语提供了 estimate 与 esteem。

items.en: Old French aesmer, also written esmer, developed the senses 'to estimate, to guess, to aim'; the exact route from valuing to aiming is generally accepted but the details are debated.
items.cn: 古法语 aesmer（亦写作 esmer）发展出「估量、推测、瞄准」等义；从「估价」到「瞄准」的路径一般认为成立，但具体细节仍有争论。

items.en: The verb entered English in the Middle English period with both the estimating and the pointing senses still alive.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语时期进入英语，「估量」与「对准」两个意思当时都还活着。

items.en: The noun aim is recorded later, from the verb, and settles into the sense of a purpose or a mark to be hit.
items.cn: 名词 aim 出现较晚，由动词而来，逐渐固定为「目的」或「要击中的标记」。

items.en: The purpose sense now dominates in ordinary use, while take aim keeps the old bodily picture of a weapon held steady.
items.cn: 现代英语里「目的」义在日常使用中占主导，而 take aim 仍保留着端稳武器那个身体画面。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin root or the same English stem; the second group holds the nouns and verbs that overlap with aim in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组由同一拉丁词根或同一英语词干构成；第二组是意思与 aim 重叠的名词与动词。

entries.definition: Without a purpose or direction; the -less suffix removes exactly what aim supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无目标的、漫无目的的」，后缀 -less 正好去掉了 aim 所提供的东西。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no purpose, as in walking aimlessly through the streets.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「漫无目的地」，如毫无目标地在街上走。

entries.definition: To judge an amount or value roughly; it shares the Latin root aestimare with aim but kept the valuing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「估计、估算」，与 aim 同出拉丁词根 aestimare，但保留了「估量价值」的意思。

entries.definition: To respect or value highly; another descendant of aestimare, with worth turned into personal regard.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊重、敬重」，也是 aestimare 的后代，只是把「价值」转成了对人的看重。

entries.definition: The result a person or team works toward; often a single concrete end, as in a career goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，常指单一而具体的结果，如职业目标。

entries.definition: A mark to be hit, or a figure to be reached; it keeps more of the physical shooting image than aim does.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「靶子、指标」，比 aim 保留了更多「射击靶标」的实体意象。

entries.definition: The reason why something is done; it explains motive rather than naming the result to be reached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目的、用意」，解释的是做事的理由，而不是要抵达的结果。

entries.definition: A stated result that an organisation plans to reach; formal and often measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标、指标」，指机构计划达成的明确结果，语气正式，常可量化。

entries.definition: What a person means to do; it stays inside the mind and makes no claim that anything was hit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意图」，指人打算做什么，停留在心里，并不表示真的击中了什么。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases in which aim does its daily work.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用的是真实的拉丁词根，以及 aim 日常真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Aestimare is to judge a distance and a value: an archer estimates before releasing, and that estimate became aim.
normal.cn: aestimare 是估量距离与价值：射手放箭前先估量，这份估量就变成了 aim。

normal.en: Estimate and esteem are cousins: same root, one still counts, one still values.
normal.cn: estimate 与 esteem 是表亲：同一个词根，一个还在数，一个还在看重。

normal.en: Take aim keeps the body in the word: hands steady, eye on the mark.
normal.cn: take aim 把身体留在词里：手要稳，眼要看住标记。

normal.en: Aim at is for a target; aim to is for a plan.
normal.cn: aim at 对着靶子，aim to 对着计划。

normal.en: The -less in aimless simply removes the target and leaves the walking.
normal.cn: aimless 里的 -less 只是拿掉了靶子，留下还在走的人。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room with one lit point on the far wall: everything you do turns until it lines up with that point.
abstract.cn: 想象一间黑屋子，远墙上只有一个亮点：你做的每件事都在转动，直到与那个点连成一线。

abstract.en: The point can be a deer, a star, a market or a child's future; only the distance changes.
abstract.cn: 那个点可以是鹿、星星、市场，也可以是孩子的未来；变的只是距离。

abstract.en: Aim is always a line, never the impact: it stops at the moment of lining up.
abstract.cn: aim 永远是一条线，而不是撞击：它停在「对准」那一刻。

examples.en: Our aim is to cut waste by half this year.
examples.cn: 我们的目标是今年把浪费减少一半。

examples.en: She aimed the camera at the children playing by the river.
examples.cn: 她把相机对准了在河边玩耍的孩子们。

examples.en: The programme aims to help farmers save water.
examples.cn: 这个项目旨在帮助农民节约用水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶姆」——拉弓时轻轻「诶」一声，姆指一松，箭朝目标去了

root: 古法语 aesmer（亦作 esmer）意为「估量、推测、瞄准」，一般认为源自拉丁语 aestimare「估价、判断价值」；由「估量距离」到「对准目标」的语义转移发生在法语阶段，名词 aim 后由动词派生。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses all keep one line: a point is chosen, and something is turned until it lines up with that point, whether the thing is an arrow, a camera, a course or a campaign.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都守着同一条线：先挑定一个点，再把某样东西转到与它连成一线；被转过去的可以是箭、相机、课程，也可以是一场宣传活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawn bow, a steady eye, and a point on the far wall that everything lines up with.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉满的弓、稳住的目光，以及远墙上那个一切都朝它对齐的点。

branches.en: THE RESULT: the point taken out of the bow becomes the goal a person wants to reach.
branches.cn: 结果线：从弓上取下来的那个点，成了人想抵达的目标。

branches.en: THE FEW SECONDS: take aim names the held moment before release, with no result yet.
branches.cn: 瞬间线：take aim 指的是放手之前那段屏住的时间，结果还没发生。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the verb turns the front end of a weapon or lens until it meets the target.
branches.cn: 器物线：动词把武器或镜头的前端转过去，直到与目标相接。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a goal inside the mind is aimed at by a course of action, so pointing becomes intending.
branches.cn: 计划线：心里的目标由一系列行动去对准，于是「瞄准」变成「旨在」。

branches.en: THE AUDIENCE: the paper target is replaced by people, and the line now ends at a group to be reached.
branches.cn: 受众线：纸靶换成人，这条线的终点变成了一群要被触达的人。

intro.en: Aim is a borrowed verb whose Latin root still shows through in estimate and esteem; English builds its own small family on top.
intro.cn: aim 是一个借入的动词，它的拉丁词根仍能从 estimate 与 esteem 看出来；英语在它上面又长出一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Aestimare and its noun aestimatio are recorded Latin; the further origin of the root is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: aestimare 及其名词 aestimatio 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.exampleCN: 它经古法语进入英语。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根留在 estimate 与 esteem 里。

definition_zh: 空气；空中；航空；播送；神态；气氛；曲调；晾晒、通风
definition_en: the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth, the space above the ground, a manner or mood that seems to float around a person or place, or to dry and freshen something by exposure to it
core_image: 推开窗，一股看不见的流动穿过房间，把窗帘轻轻掀起
scene: 雨后的小院里，床单挂在竹竿上，风从巷口穿过来回摆动。We opened every window to air the rooms before the family arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 air 是「通风、晾一晾」（第 7 个义项：让空气流通以去除潮气或异味）；句意为我们在家人到来前打开所有窗户给房间通风。画面里是小院、竹竿上的床单与穿巷的风。

pos.zh: 名词：空气；空中；播送；神态；气氛；曲调
动词：晾晒；通风

collocations.zh: 在空中；弥漫着某种气氛

derivatives.zh: 由 air 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「通风的、轻飘飘的、不着边际的」
由 air 加后缀 -less 构成，义为「无空气的、不通风的」
由拉丁语 aer「空气」加动词后缀构成，义为「使通气、给……充气」
由拉丁语 aer 加形容词后缀构成，义为「空中的、航空的」，作名词指天线

senses.title: The gas mixture we breathe
senses.definition: the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth and that people, animals and plants breathe
senses.definitionCN: 包围地球、供人、动物与植物呼吸的混合气体
senses.example: The mountain air was so cold that every breath came out as mist.
senses.exampleCN: 山上的空气冷得让每一次呼吸都化成白雾。
senses.why: Greek aer named the lower, misty layer near the ground; that moist stuff you can feel but not see is the word's oldest and most physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 aer 本指地面附近那层带雾气的下层气；这种能感到却看不见的潮湿之物，正是这个词最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: The space above the ground
senses.definition: the open space above the ground, or travel and transport through that space
senses.definitionCN: 地面上方的开阔空间，或经由这片空间的旅行与运输
senses.example: The package will go by air and arrive within two days.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹将走航空，两天内到达。
senses.why: The same substance fills the whole space above us, so the word for the gas also names the open region a plane moves through.
senses.whyCN: 同一种物质铺满了我们头顶的整个空间，于是指这种气体的词也用来指飞机穿行的那片开阔区域。

senses.title: Being broadcast
senses.definition: the sending out of radio or television signals, or the state of being broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 无线电或电视信号的发送，或处于被播出的状态
senses.example: The interview will be on the air at nine tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 这段采访今晚九点播出。
senses.why: Radio sends sound through the air with no wire, so the medium itself became the name of the act; on the air is literally riding the air.
senses.whyCN: 无线电让声音不靠导线而从空气中穿过，介质本身就成了动作的名称；on the air 字面上就是「乘着空气」。

senses.title: A manner or appearance
senses.definition: the way a person looks or behaves, especially when it suggests a feeling or quality
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的神情或举止，尤指其中透出的感受或气质
senses.example: He answered with an air of quiet confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着一种沉静自信的神态作答。
senses.why: Old French used air for the look a face carries; like the atmosphere around a body, a manner is something you sense before you can name it.
senses.whyCN: 古法语用 air 指脸上带着的那层神色；就像人身周围的气氛，神态也是你先感到、后才会命名的东西。

senses.title: The mood of a place
senses.definition: the feeling or mood that a place or situation seems to have
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方或一种情境似乎带有的感觉与情绪
senses.example: An air of tension filled the courtroom before the verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 宣判前，法庭里弥漫着紧张的气氛。
senses.why: A room's air is shared by everyone in it, so the word widens from a person's manner to the mood that hangs over a whole space.
senses.whyCN: 一间屋子的空气由里面所有人共同呼吸，于是这个词从一个人的神态扩展到笼罩整个空间的情绪。

senses.title: A simple tune
senses.definition: a simple melody, especially one in older or Baroque music
senses.definitionCN: 简单的旋律，尤指早期或巴洛克音乐中的短曲
senses.example: The violinist played a slow air by Purcell.
senses.exampleCN: 小提琴手演奏了一首普塞尔的缓慢曲调。
senses.why: A melody is shaped air: breath moving through an instrument, and the older musical use named the moving breath rather than the notes.
senses.whyCN: 旋律就是被塑形的空气：气息穿过乐器；旧时的音乐用法命名的是这股流动的气息，而不是纸上的音符。

senses.title: To dry or freshen by exposure
senses.definition: to put clothes, bedding or a room where moving air can dry or freshen it
senses.definitionCN: 把衣物、被褥或房间置于流动空气中，使其干燥或清新
senses.example: She aired the blankets on the balcony before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到来前，她把毯子晾在阳台上透气。
senses.why: Once air is a thing you can stand in, the verb is simply putting an object into it and letting the movement do the work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦空气成了可以置身其中的东西，动词就只是把物件放进空气里，让流动自己去干活。

intro.en: Air is a Greek word that travelled through Latin and Old French; the same noun then split into gas, sky, manner, mood and melody.
intro.cn: air 是一个希腊词，经拉丁语与古法语传下来；同一个名词随后分化出气体、天空、神态、气氛与曲调等意思。

items.en: Greek aer named the lower, misty air near the earth, as opposed to aither, the bright upper sky; the contrast is generally accepted.
items.cn: 希腊语 aer 指地面附近那层带雾气的下层空气，与指明亮上层的 aither 相对；这一对立关系一般认为成立。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer from Greek with the same meaning, and the word appears in learned compounds such as aerius, 'of the air'.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 aer，意思不变；这个词也出现在 aerius「空气的」这类书面复合形式中。

items.en: Old French air carried both 'atmosphere' and 'appearance, manner', the second sense growing from the look a face wears.
items.cn: 古法语 air 同时带「大气」与「外貌、神态」两义，后一义由脸上的神色生长出来。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the Middle English period and kept the physical and the facial senses side by side.
items.cn: 英语在中古英语时期借入这个词，物理义与面部神态义并行保留。

items.en: Wireless broadcasting gave on the air in the twentieth century; the musical sense came through French and Italian forms of the same Latin word, though the exact path of that shift is source uncertain.
items.cn: 无线电广播在二十世纪带来 on the air 的说法；音乐义则经同一拉丁词的法语与意大利语形式而来，但这一语义转移的确切路径来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is built on the Greek and Latin root for air; the second group holds the substances, spaces and moods that air is commonly confused with.
note.cn: 第一组建立在表示「空气」的希腊语与拉丁语词根上；第二组收的是常与 air 混淆的物质、空间与情绪。

entries.definition: Full of fresh air, or light and careless in manner; the -y suffix turns the noun into a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「通风的」或「轻飘飘的、漫不经心的」，后缀 -y 把名词变成性质。

entries.definition: With no moving air and no fresh supply of it; the -less suffix denies exactly what air provides.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不通风的、没有新鲜空气的」，后缀 -less 正好否定了 air 提供的东西。

entries.definition: Of or in the air, or a device for receiving signals; it comes from Latin aerius, from the same aer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「空中的、航空的」，作名词指天线；源自拉丁语 aerius，与 air 同出 aer。

entries.definition: To expose something to air or force air into it, as with soil or water.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使通气、给……充气」，如给土壤或水通气。

entries.definition: The whole layer of gases around a planet, or the mood of a place; wider in the first sense than air.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「大气层」或「氛围」；作「大气」时范围比 air 更大，作「氛围」时与 air 的第五义相近。

entries.definition: A light wind; it names moving air, not the substance itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微风」，指流动起来的空气，而不是空气这种物质本身。

entries.definition: Air moving across the earth's surface; stronger and more directional than a breeze.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风」，指沿地表流动的空气，比微风更强，方向性也更明显。

entries.definition: One gas among those in air, the one animals need to breathe; a chemical element, not a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「氧气」，是空气成分之一、动物呼吸所需的气体，属化学元素而非混合物。

entries.definition: The space you see above the earth; a visual expanse rather than the gas that fills it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天空」，指你在地面上方看见的那片空间，是视觉上的辽阔，而非充塞其中的气体。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Greek root, the everyday phrases and the visible behaviour of the substance itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子顺着希腊词根、日常搭配，以及这种物质本身看得见的表现。

normal.en: Aer is the damp lower air; aerial and aerate both keep that root alive.
normal.cn: aer 是潮湿的下层空气；aerial 与 aerate 都让这个词根活着。

normal.en: On the air means riding the air: sound with no wire under it.
normal.cn: on the air 就是乘着空气：底下没有导线的声音。

normal.en: By air moves a parcel from truck to plane without changing the word.
normal.cn: by air 把包裹从卡车换到飞机，词本身却一点没变。

normal.en: Put on airs is to wear a manner the way you wear a coat.
normal.cn: put on airs 是把神态当作外套穿在身上，也就是摆架子。

normal.en: An air in music is breath shaped into a tune.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 air 是被塑造成曲调的一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a window opened in a stuffy room: nothing visible enters, yet the curtains move and the room changes.
abstract.cn: 想象闷屋子里推开一扇窗：没有看得见的东西进来，窗帘却动了，屋子也变了。

abstract.en: The same invisible movement can carry a voice, a mood or a melody; only what it carries changes.
abstract.cn: 同一股看不见的流动可以载声音、载情绪、载旋律；变的只是它所承载的东西。

abstract.en: Air is the one thing you are always inside, which is why it can name both the world and a look on a face.
abstract.cn: 空气是你始终身处其中的那样东西，正因如此它既能命名世界，也能命名脸上的一层神色。

examples.en: The air in the cellar smelled of wet wood.
examples.cn: 地窖里的空气有一股湿木头的气味。

examples.en: The concert will be on the air at eight.
examples.cn: 这场音乐会将在八点播出。

examples.en: He spoke with the air of a man who had never been refused.
examples.cn: 他说话时带着一种从未被人拒绝过的神态。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶尔」——推开窗「诶」一声，一股气流就进来了

root: 希腊语 aer 指地面附近带雾气的下层空气，与指明亮上层的 aither 相对；经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 进入英语，由「气」引申出空中、播送、神态、气氛与曲调。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all come from one invisible substance: what you breathe, the space it fills, the signals it carries, the manner it seems to wrap around a person, the mood it gives a room, the breath shaped into a tune, and the act of letting it move through things.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都出自同一种看不见的物质：你呼吸的东西、它充满的空间、它承载的信号、它仿佛裹在人身上的神态、它给一间屋子的气氛、被塑成曲调的气息，以及让它在物件间流动的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible flow that fills every open space and moves whatever it touches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的流动，填满每一处开阔空间，并推动它所触到的一切。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the damp gas near the ground that every breath takes in.
branches.cn: 物质线：地面附近那层潮湿的气体，每一次呼吸都把它吸进去。

branches.en: THE SPACE: because the gas fills the region above us, the word also names that region and travel through it.
branches.cn: 空间线：因为这种气充满我们头顶的区域，这个词也用来指那片区域与穿越它的旅行。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: sound and pictures ride the air without wires, so the medium became the act of broadcasting.
branches.cn: 信号线：声音与图像不靠导线而乘着空气，于是介质本身成了「播送」这个动作。

branches.en: THE MANNER: what hangs around a person or a room is felt before it is named, first as a look, then as a mood.
branches.cn: 神态线：绕在人身旁或屋子里的东西总先被感到、后被命名，先是个人的神色，后是空间的气氛。

branches.en: THE BREATH: breath shaped by an instrument becomes a tune, while letting air move through cloth or a room becomes the verb.
branches.cn: 气息线：气息被乐器塑形就成了曲调，而让空气穿过布料或房间就成了动词「晾晒、通风」。

intro.en: Air is a Greek root that Latin and French passed on, and English builds a wide family of compounds and suffixes on it.
intro.cn: air 是一个经拉丁语与法语传下来的希腊词根，英语在它上面长出了大量复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aer and the adjective aerius are recorded borrowings from Greek; the Greek noun itself is attested, and only its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aer 与形容词 aerius 都是有记录的希腊语借词；希腊语名词本身有文献，只是更早的来源不确定。
